bullets: Existing models often fail on sparse, large-step camera trajectories, producing frozen frames, inaccurate motion, and geometric drift.
DTTD interpolates sparse camera paths into dense trajectories that the frozen base model can reliably generate.
Pose-aligned dense teacher videos supervise candidate outputs generated on the original sparse trajectory, without extra data or an external teacher.
Geometry-aware rewards measure cross-frame consistency and trajectory following for offline preference optimization.
A cumulative curriculum progressively increases motion difficulty while retaining simpler trajectories to limit capability forgetting.
papers.selection_reason: Post-training framework to extend video world models to large camera motions via dense teacher distillation.
papers.title: Distilling Dense Trajectory Teachers For Large-Motion Video World Models
papers.tldr: DTTD extends video world models from small to large camera motions by using dense-trajectory self-teaching, geometry-aware rewards, and curriculum-based preference optimization.

papers.abstract: Controlling the camera relative to a moving subject in an existing video is challenging: behaviors such as maintaining a frontal view require the camera to adapt to the subject's changing position and orientation, making the desired trajectory difficult to specify in advance. Existing camera-controlled video-to-video methods typically rely on explicit trajectories or reference motions, which do not directly express these dynamic camera--subject relationships. We introduce semantic camera motion control, a novel video-to-video task in which a reference video and a target motion label specify the desired subject-relative camera behavior without an explicit target trajectory. Our method, SemCam, learns to realize this behavior while preserving source content. It combines shared-basis low-rank adaptation with motion-conditioned modulation, while a background-consistency loss encourages fidelity in regions visible in both reference and target videos. We construct 661 paired videos covering eight semantic camera behaviors and evaluate on a separate 109-scene benchmark using subject-relative motion metrics, appearance measures, and a user study. SemCam achieves a semantic-motion success rate of 68.6%, compared with 45.3% for Vista4D, the strongest evaluated baseline, while maintaining comparable subject identity preservation.
bullets: Addresses the difficulty of specifying camera motion around subjects whose position and orientation change over time.
Uses a reference video plus a target motion label to express behaviors such as maintaining a frontal view.
Combines shared-basis low-rank adaptation, motion-conditioned modulation, and a background-consistency loss.
Evaluated on 661 paired videos and a separate 109-scene benchmark covering eight semantic camera behaviors.
Outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline on semantic-motion success while maintaining comparable subject identity preservation.
papers.selection_reason: Semantic camera-motion control for video generation via motion-conditioned adaptation and background consistency.
papers.title: SemCam: Semantic Camera Motion Control for Video Generation
papers.tldr: SemCam enables semantic, subject-relative camera control in video generation without requiring an explicit target trajectory, achieving a 68.6% semantic-motion success rate while preserving subject identity.

papers.abstract: Continuous visual world simulation requires coupling evolving scene geometry with temporally persistent appearance. We present UniWorld, a unified framework that integrates depth trajectories and reference appearance within a shared video generation model. The central design maintains visual and geometric histories on a common timeline. Noise-aligned overlapping continuation places generated history at the prescribed sampling noise level and commits only newly generated latents. Rolling depth latent state preserves the corresponding geometric controls, incrementally reads newly available geometry, and keeps the conditioning fixed within each sampling window. Together, these mechanisms ensure exact preservation of latent history while bounding the active depth state by the window size. We evaluate continuous generation, paired history interventions, and long-horizon behavior across diverse scene categories. The same generator supports estimated, native, and on-demand simulator depth, while cached and incremental execution paths produce bitwise-identical outputs. Appearance changes and geometric control branches operate through the same interface without modifying committed history. The measured steady-state DiT execution path achieves real-time generation throughput, demonstrating the efficiency of UniWorld for continuous visual world simulation.
authors: Xin Zhang, Yabo Chen, Shuaiwei Wang, Zixuan Duan, Haibin Huang, Feng Xu, Xuelong Li
bullets: Addresses the challenge of coupling temporally persistent visual appearance with changing scene geometry.
Uses noise-aligned overlapping continuation to preserve generated latent history while committing only new content.
Maintains rolling depth latents and fixed per-window conditioning to control geometry with bounded active state.
Supports estimated, native, and on-demand simulator depth, with cached and incremental execution producing identical outputs.
Evaluations cover continuous generation, history interventions, and long-horizon behavior across diverse scenes; the steady-state DiT path achieves real-time throughput.
papers.selection_reason: Continuous visual world simulation via a unified video generation model with depth and appearance histories; directly fits world models and video diffusion.
papers.title: UniWorld: A Unified World Model for Real-Time Visual World Simulation
papers.tldr: UniWorld enables real-time, continuous visual world simulation by jointly maintaining persistent appearance and evolving scene geometry in a unified video generator.

papers.abstract: Generating multiple videos of a dynamic scene from a single reference video requires synthesizing both observed and unobserved content consistently across viewpoints. Existing camera-control methods for video diffusion typically rely on architectural mechanisms, including camera embeddings, cross-view attention, and geometric conditioning. Although effective for static scene content, these approaches often struggle with the fine-grained, dynamic geometry that must remain coherent across views and over time. We synchronize the diffusion process itself by sampling the Gaussian noise prior in a canonical 3D space derived from the source video and rasterizing it into target cameras, rather than sampling independently in each 2D image plane. Our method, SyncVid, lifts a monocular video into a canonical 4D representation, associates noise with scene geometry and unseen space, and rasterizes the resulting structured noise into arbitrary views. Because rendering can introduce local correlations, we further propose a cross-view-consistent whitening procedure that decorrelates neighboring pixels while preserving correspondence across views. The structured noise serves as the diffusion prior for a LoRA-adapted pretrained video diffusion model, requiring no architectural modifications. By enforcing spatiotemporal and cross-view coherence at the source of stochasticity, SyncVid generates synchronized videos and improves both perceptual quality and cross-view consistency in our experiments. Project page: https://qualcomm-ai-research.github.io/SyncVid-Webpage.
authors: Farhad G. Zanjani, Animesh Karnewar, Fatih Porikli, Amirhossein Habibian
bullets: Addresses the challenge of generating temporally and cross-view coherent videos from a single reference video, especially for dynamic geometry.
Lifts the source video into a canonical 4D representation and rasterizes geometry-aware noise into target camera views.
Introduces cross-view-consistent whitening to reduce local correlations while preserving correspondence across views.
Uses the structured noise as the prior for a LoRA-adapted pretrained video diffusion model without architectural modifications.
Experiments report improved perceptual quality and cross-view consistency, though the abstract provides no quantitative results.
papers.selection_reason: World-equivariant diffusion noise for synchronized multi-view video generation; directly advances diffusion-based video generation with cross-view consistency.
papers.title: SyncVid: World-Equivariant Diffusion for Synchronized Video Generation
papers.tldr: SyncVid synchronizes multi-view video generation by coordinating diffusion noise in a canonical 3D space, improving visual quality and cross-view consistency without changing the model architecture.

papers.abstract: Video diffusion models have learned rich 3D/4D priors, making them promising for scene generation and video re-rendering. However, their use in spatial tasks is limited by imprecise camera control, spatial and temporal inconsistencies, and entangled camera motion with scene dynamics. Existing approaches, such as task-specific fine-tuning and post-process warping, often introduce visual artifacts, generalize poorly, or incur high computational costs. We propose WorldForge V2 to achieve accurate camera control while preserving the generative capabilities of pretrained video models. We first develop a training-free guidance framework using warped references to iteratively refine generation along a target camera path. Optical-flow analysis identifies motion-related latent channels for selective guidance, helping separate motion control from appearance. A dual-path strategy further compares guided and unguided predictions to correct artifacts from imperfect references. Together, these components guide viewpoint changes while preserving scene appearance and object motion. To reduce refinement costs, v-cache approximates the correction using the preceding denoising prediction, avoiding an additional model evaluation. We further extend motion localization from latent channels to network blocks and introduce Trajectory LoRA, which concentrates adaptation on blocks most responsive to trajectory guidance. A two-stage training strategy teaches these adapters to denoise the states encountered during guided generation, using limited supervision effectively. This enables reliable camera control with very little training data, with a single training scene already supporting generalization to unseen scenes. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations across multiple datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art generation quality and trajectory accuracy in camera-controlled video generation.
authors: Chenxi Song, Yanming Yang, Tong Zhao, Ruibo Li, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Chi Zhang
bullets: Addresses imprecise camera control, temporal/spatial inconsistencies, and entanglement between camera motion and scene dynamics.
Uses warped-reference guidance, optical-flow-based motion localization, and dual-path prediction to refine generation along target camera paths.
Introduces v-cache to reduce refinement cost and Trajectory LoRA to adapt only trajectory-responsive network blocks.
A two-stage training strategy enables reliable control with limited supervision; one training scene can generalize to unseen scenes.
Experiments across multiple datasets report state-of-the-art camera trajectory accuracy and generation quality.
papers.selection_reason: Camera-controlled video diffusion with trajectory guidance and efficient refinement.
papers.title: WorldForge V2: Eliciting Camera-Trajectory Alignment in Video Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: WorldForge V2 improves camera-trajectory control in video diffusion models while preserving scene appearance and object motion, using training-free guidance plus targeted lightweight adaptation.

papers.abstract: AI coding agents can now build small playable games in minutes, but the results usually look like programmer art: gray blockouts, colored geometric primitives, and flat semantic blobs. We present AnyGameRenderer, a video-to-video generative renderer that turns such footage into high-quality visuals with characters, motion detail, and effects. Throughout, it keeps the layout, camera, and every entity's position and timing intact. Our AnyGameRenderer generalizes across a wide range of genres that agents build, such as tower defense, auto-battlers, top-down survivors, turn-based battles, kart racing, and crowd runners. AnyGameRenderer takes plain video as its game-state input, with no complex representations such as engine G-buffers, per-object class labels, or low-poly proxies. Gray blockouts, colored primitives, semantic maps, and wireframes all work as input. It also preserves entity correspondence: group counts stay correct, and entities appear and disappear on the right frame. We implement AnyGameRenderer by LoRA fine-tuning MiniMax-H3 ref2va, a 33B reference-video-conditioned video generation model. Training uses $\sim$10k paired clips from three sources: (i) multi-stream rendering data from 38 agent-made games exported from GEAR, an AI game-creation tool; (ii) two-stream rendering data from Unreal Engine, with programmatically controlled crowds, count changes, and entity scales; and (iii) real gameplay recordings, with pairs reconstructed via 3D-box detection. To evaluate the entity correspondence, we propose an entity-level benchmark of 59 held-out cases with 753 entities, scored against ground-truth boxes. Compared with the base model, AnyGameRenderer better preserves entity correspondence: temporal match rises from 50.9\% to 62.9\%, missed count changes fall from 34.7\% to 21.3\%, and fewer entities are hallucinated or left unrendered.
authors: Ruicong Liu, Liangyang Ouyang, Fengbo Lan, Zhixiang Wang, Kaipeng Zhang
bullets: Addresses programmer-art visuals produced by AI-built games.
Uses video-to-video generation from plain footage, without G-buffers, object labels, or 3D proxies.
LoRA-fine-tunes a reference-video-conditioned video model on paired game-rendering clips and gameplay recordings.
Introduces an entity-level benchmark with 59 held-out cases and 753 entities.
Improves temporal entity matching from 50.9% to 62.9% and reduces missed count changes from 34.7% to 21.3% versus the base model.
papers.selection_reason: Entity-consistent video-to-video generative rendering, relevant to video generation and editing.
papers.title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark
papers.tldr: AnyGameRenderer converts simple game footage into detailed visuals while preserving each entity’s position, timing, appearance, and count across diverse game genres.

papers.abstract: Cinematic video generation requires both temporal inference from limited inputs (i.e., sparse rather than frame-by-frame guidance) and factor-aware control of character, scene, action, and camera. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer useful priors for both capabilities, but their representations are not automatically actionable for video generation: a Video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) may bypass them through native conditioning pathways, and using them does not ensure either factor-aware control or generation-compatible temporal prediction. We propose Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL), which establishes effective MLLM latent use as a shared prerequisite and then targets the two capabilities with complementary learning signals. First, latent-only generator grounding trains the DiT with a frozen MLLM and connector, strengthening the DiT's use of MLLM latents for generation. Second, for factor-aware control, paired videos specify a target-factor change and non-target preservation, and factor-span replacement trains the DiT to realize this relationship in its output. Third, for temporal inference, text-only and text-plus-complete-video observations share a video target, and the trained DiT is then frozen while the MLLM and connector are optimized through it. This final stage trains limited-input representations for generation while retaining complete-observation reconstruction as a complementary training mode. Extensive experiments demonstrate our consistently better performance on three cinematic video generation tasks (i.e., sparse-to-video, factor-aware editing, and multi-shot generation) over baselines and validate FAPL's contributions to MLLM feature use, temporal control, and factor coordination.
authors: Songlin Yang, Zhe Wang, Xiaotong Zhao, Xi Wang, Ran Zhang, Shuai Li, Taiyi Wu, Songlian Li, Eric Liu, Alan Zhao, Anyi Rao
bullets: Addresses the gap between useful MLLM representations and their reliable use by video diffusion transformers.
Uses latent-only generator grounding to make the DiT depend on frozen MLLM latents.
Learns factor-aware editing through paired videos with target-factor changes and non-target preservation.
Trains temporal inference from text or incomplete video by optimizing the MLLM and connector through a frozen DiT.
Reports consistently better performance than baselines across sparse-to-video, factor-aware editing, and multi-shot generation tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Cinematic video generation with MLLM latent grounding and factor-aware control fits diffusion video generation interests.
papers.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
papers.tldr: FAPL trains MLLM latents to become actionable for cinematic video generation with sparse temporal guidance and factor-aware control.

papers.abstract: Diffusion-based audio-visual generation methods typically perform joint denoising of audio and video latents throughout the entire sampling trajectory, repeatedly executing modality-specific denoising branches and cross-modal attention at every timestep. However, we observe that such uniform joint computation is not always necessary. The key is a modality-asymmetric recoverability: audio-side drift introduced by mid-stage caching can be substantially reduced by only a few terminal joint denoising steps, whereas video-side degradation caused by caching leads to persistent loss of motion and temporal details. This asymmetry suggests that inference acceleration should selectively cache recoverable audio-side computation while preserving full video refinement. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Convergence-Adaptive Audio-Visual Cache (CAVC)}, a training-free modality-asymmetric caching framework. CAVC adopts a sandwich-structured computation allocation: after detecting that audio denoiser outputs enter a cache-tolerant regime, it caches and reuses the audio denoiser output to bypass audio denoising and cross-modal attention in the middle stage, while the video branch continues independent spatio-temporal refinement; a few joint steps are then restored at the end to reduce accumulated cross-modal drift and improve synchronization. Experiments across multiple public benchmarks demonstrate that CAVC achieves 1.10--1.35x wall-clock acceleration, improves several visual dynamics and temporal statistics, and maintains competitive audio fidelity and audio-visual alignment.
authors: Lifan Jiang, Yibo Zhao, Senlin cheng, Bolei Xu, Xiaobo Li, Can Ye, Dehai Zhao, Deng Cai, Boxi Wu
bullets: Addresses unnecessary joint audio-video denoising and cross-modal attention at every sampling step.
Uses a training-free, convergence-adaptive cache with sandwich-structured computation allocation.
Caches audio denoiser outputs in a cache-tolerant middle regime while video undergoes full spatio-temporal refinement.
Restores a few terminal joint denoising steps to reduce cross-modal drift and improve synchronization.

Across public benchmarks, achieves 1.10–1.35× wall-clock acceleration while maintaining competitive audio fidelity and audio-visual alignment and improving several visual dynamics and temporal statistics.
papers.selection_reason: Accelerates audio-visual diffusion generation via modality-asymmetric caching, relevant to video diffusion and inference efficiency.
papers.title: CAVC: Convergence-Adaptive Audio-Visual Cache for Modality-Asymmetric Diffusion Generation
papers.tldr: CAVC accelerates audio-visual diffusion generation by caching recoverable audio computation mid-sampling while preserving video refinement and restoring joint denoising at the end.

papers.abstract: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have substantially improved visual fidelity, yet existing models still struggle to understand the physical evolution implicit in user prompts, making it difficult to generate videos with continuous physical state evolution. Here, we propose PhyEvolve, a multi-agent framework that enhances natural-language prompts through structured state-evolution planning. PhyEvolve consists of three agents: a Director, a Physical Evolver, and a Composer. Given a user prompt and an optional first frame, the Director grounds the scene and disentangles physical events from observation changes. The Physical Evolver uses scene evidence to identify physical mechanisms then constructs causally linked state transitions that unfold throughout the video, whether visible or not. The Composer utilizes these transitions to enhance the original prompts. Without retraining or model modification, PhyEvolve works directly with existing generators through prompt replacement. Extensive experiments on four major benchmarks show that PhyEvolve achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming the cutting-edge prior agentic baseline by 7.9 percentage points on average. These results demonstrate that explicit causal state-evolution planning improves physical consistency and state continuity in generated videos through natural-language prompt enhancement.
authors: Yang-Hao Zhou, Lixing Tan, Zhiqi Li, Guang Yang, Xiao Yang
bullets: Addresses poor modeling of continuous physical evolution in text-to-video generation.
Uses three agents: Director, Physical Evolver, and Composer.
Plans causally linked physical state transitions, including changes that may not be directly visible.
Works with existing video generators through prompt replacement and optional first-frame input.
Evaluated on four benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art results and a 7.9-point average gain over a prior agentic baseline.
papers.selection_reason: Agentic prompt planning for physics-aware text-to-video generation improves video diffusion outputs.
papers.title: PhyEvolve: Multi-Agent State-Evolution Planning for Physics-Aware Video Generation
papers.tldr: PhyEvolve improves physics-aware video generation by using multi-agent causal state-evolution planning to enhance prompts without modifying or retraining the video generator.

papers.abstract: Adding control to video generation often requires training, which demands additional computational resources, data, or architectural changes. We propose a training-free approach that utilizes pretrained video diffusion models to control object layout and motion using coarse layouts. Our method operates in two passes: first, it steers spatiotemporal placement through prompt-guided cross-attention to produce a coarse visual guide; second, this guide conditions the same model to generate a high-quality, layoutconsistent video. The approach enables coordinated motion with strong temporal consistency, supporting diverse trajectories and object interactions without additional training. Extensive experiments show that our method consistently outperforms prior work in overlap and trajectory accuracy, as well as visual quality across static, dynamic, and multi-object scene settings.
authors: Asaf Joseph, Moshe Mandel, Ohad Fried
bullets: Addresses the computational and architectural costs of training-based video-generation control.
Uses prompt-guided cross-attention to create a coarse spatiotemporal visual guide.
Conditions the same pretrained model on this guide to generate layout-consistent videos.
Supports diverse trajectories, coordinated motion, and multi-object interactions without additional training.
Experiments report improved overlap, trajectory accuracy, and visual quality across static and dynamic scenes.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free layout-guided control of pretrained video diffusion models for temporally consistent video synthesis; fits video generation interests.
papers.title: Latent Space Jam: Layout Guided Video Synthesis
papers.tldr: A training-free two-pass method controls object layouts and motion in pretrained video diffusion models while preserving temporal consistency and visual quality.

papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of creating immersive volumetric videos from sparse and low-resolution capture resources. Conventional dense multi-view reconstruction methods can produce high-quality volumetric videos, but their reliance on costly capture setups makes them impractical in real-world scenarios. Recent approaches use generative models to relax capture requirements, but still suffer from limited resolution and 4D inconsistency. To overcome these constraints, we propose RealMe, a unified framework built around a high-resolution video diffusion model that enhances limited captures into high-resolution (2K), 4D-consistent videos for volumetric video reconstruction. Specifically, RealMe constructs auxiliary data from capture videos and encodes them into latents along with layout-aware positional embeddings. The video diffusion model adapts factorized spatio-temporal attention to the multi-view capture layout, denoises these latents across viewpoints and time, and decodes them into enhanced videos to refine the 4D representation. This adaptation helps the model capture temporal dynamics and multi-view relationships, leading to more 4D-consistent generation. To reduce the data gap between generated videos and real captures, we apply a latent frequency loss that provides frequency-domain supervision in latent space. Extensive experiments on the public DNA-Rendering benchmark and our self-captured RealVV dataset demonstrate that RealMe is able to create immersive volumetric videos and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in visual fidelity and 4D consistency.
authors: Chenxu Zhou, Zhiyuan Yu, Yudong Jin, Yinji Shentu, Yu Zhang, Jiaming Sun, Xiaowei Zhou
bullets: Targets costly dense multi-view capture requirements and the limited resolution and 4D consistency of prior generative methods.
Builds auxiliary data from capture videos and combines latent representations with layout-aware positional embeddings.
Adapts factorized spatio-temporal attention to model relationships across viewpoints and time.
Uses latent frequency-domain supervision to reduce the gap between generated videos and real captures.
Experiments on DNA-Rendering and the self-captured RealVV dataset show improved visual fidelity and 4D consistency over existing methods.
papers.selection_reason: Unified video diffusion framework for enhancing sparse multi-view captures into 4D-consistent volumetric video; directly relevant to video diffusion and 3D video generation.
papers.title: RealMe: Immersive Volumetric Video from Minimal Captures
papers.tldr: RealMe uses a high-resolution video diffusion model to turn sparse, low-resolution captures into immersive, temporally and multi-view consistent volumetric videos.

papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve. Under teacher forcing, strong temporal redundancy may allow local visual continuity to serve as a shortcut for current-chunk denoising, reducing the pressure to model visual evolution. We introduce Future Chunk Prediction (FCP), an auxiliary objective jointly optimized with teacher-forced denoising that predicts temporally separated chunks without access to the intervening visual context. Drawing supervision directly from training videos, FCP requires no additional pretrained visual encoder and leaves autoregressive inference unchanged. Our method achieves superior physical plausibility over standard teacher-forced autoregressive training with a lower overall training compute budget, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of future-chunk supervision for modeling visual evolution. Intriguingly, our visualizations suggest that FCP fosters a more structured representation space, which may be valuable for building autoregressive world models.
authors: Ruopeng Gao, Yukun Huang, Jiarui Hu, Shuai Wang, Wenbo Hu, Ying Shan, Limin Wang
bullets: Teacher forcing can exploit temporal redundancy, favoring local continuity over genuine modeling of visual evolution.
FCP adds an auxiliary future-chunk prediction objective alongside teacher-forced denoising.
The method uses training videos directly, requires no pretrained visual encoder, and does not alter inference.
It improves physical plausibility while using less overall training compute than standard teacher-forced training.
Visualizations suggest FCP produces a more structured representation space, potentially benefiting autoregressive world models.
papers.selection_reason: Future-chunk supervision for autoregressive video diffusion; fits autoregressive video generation.
papers.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.tldr: Future Chunk Prediction improves autoregressive video models’ understanding of scene evolution by training them to predict temporally separated video chunks without intervening context.

papers.abstract: Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can produce visually plausible videos, yet their camera ego-motion often drifts over long horizons. Camera ego-motion determines how the viewpoint changes between frames and is essential for maintaining consistent geometry and trajectories. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a causal alignment framework with two components. First, we diagnose how precise ego motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions, revealing a rise-and-fall pattern during denoising. Second, we strengthen ego-motion state in VGM by aligning the representations at the identified layers to a 3D foundation model through delta-token space. This space encodes the changes between consecutive frames, allowing the alignment to focus on ego-motion dynamics rather than static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign can largely improve motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness, while preserving visual quality. For example, it improves geometric consistency by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, with the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves the success rate of world action models (WAMs) by 10 points on mobile manipulation tasks of RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields noticeable gains in embodied models.
authors: Kai Zhu, Yintianrun Zhang, Shuwei Jiang, Ruolin Zuo, Yixin Chen, Duomin Wang, Miao Liu, Yin Li, Daquan Zhou, Yiwu Zhong
bullets: Targets ego-motion drift, which harms geometric and trajectory consistency in generated videos.
Uses linear probes and causal interventions to locate where ego-motion is represented, used, and retained during denoising.
Aligns representations at identified layers in delta-token space, emphasizing frame-to-frame motion changes over static scene content.
Fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K with Wan2.2, it improves motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness while preserving visual quality.
The improved video model also raises world action model success rates on RoboCasa365 mobile-manipulation tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Causal alignment of diffusion video generators for consistent ego-motion; fits video diffusion.
papers.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
papers.tldr: CausalAlign improves long-horizon camera ego-motion consistency in diffusion video generation models by causally aligning motion representations with a 3D foundation model.

papers.abstract: Understanding and modeling light transport in human-centric scenes is a longstanding challenge. While recent progress in diffusion models has boosted research in relighting, precise illumination control still lags, primarily due to the scarcity of diverse, high-quality, precisely labeled video relighting datasets. Existing end-to-end relighting approaches model light transport implicitly through neural networks, which substantially complicates controllability. In contrast, some works resort to path-traced irradiance cues as an explicit blueprint for light transport. However, such constructed irradiance cues are prone to artifacts and hinder generative quality when directly used as control signals. With the key observation that noise corruption removes high-frequency artifacts and preserves low-frequency light transport, we introduce an asynchronous joint-modeling paradigm that facilitates fine-grained illumination control. During two-stage training, we force the model to jointly denoise RGB and ground-truth irradiance frames with separate timesteps scheduling. A domain matching strategy is applied to the second stage to bridge the domain gap between irradiance cues and ground-truth irradiance maps. At inference time, we introduce an asynchronous hijacked generation pipeline that facilitates flexible illumination control. For training data, we develop a multi-illumination high-quality synthetic video dataset with paired irradiance maps using a powerful game engine. Trained exclusively on this dataset, our model exhibits robust generalization to real- world scenarios and outperforms prior approaches in both lighting fidelity and generative quality. The code and dataset will be publicly released.
authors: Henglei Lv, Bailin Deng, Xiaoqiang Liu, Yichen Wang, Haoxian Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Lin Gao
bullets: Addresses limited high-quality, precisely labeled video-relighting data and poor controllability in implicit light-transport models.
Jointly denoises RGB and ground-truth irradiance frames using separate timestep schedules across two training stages.
Uses domain matching to reduce the gap between constructed irradiance cues and ground-truth irradiance maps.
Introduces an asynchronous inference pipeline for flexible illumination control.
Trains on a synthetic multi-illumination video dataset and reportedly generalizes to real scenes, improving lighting fidelity and generative quality over prior methods.
papers.selection_reason: Diffusion-based video relighting with joint RGB-irradiance modeling, fitting video diffusion and generation interests.
papers.title: JointLight: Human-Centric Video Relighting with Asynchronous RGB-Irradiance Joint Modeling
papers.tldr: JointLight enables controllable human-centric video relighting by asynchronously modeling RGB frames and irradiance cues to preserve illumination structure while reducing cue artifacts.

papers.abstract: Full 3D attention is costly in video Diffusion Transformers. Block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only selected attention blocks. However, existing methods either overlook the potential to optimize sparsity allocation or rely on heuristic rules or local metrics to guide it. In this work, we observe that sparsifying attention in different layers and at different denoising steps affects final-video fidelity to substantially different degrees. Yet the identities of the most sensitive layer-step pairs remain nearly unchanged across inputs. Building on these findings, we propose Allocating Layer-step Latency by Output Tests (ALLOT), a training-free sparsity allocation method. Treating each layer-step pair as a cell, ALLOT estimates each cell's contribution to final-video error through (i) cell probing and (ii) trajectory calibration, then jointly optimizes cell densities under a measured-latency budget. It preserves existing selection strategies and kernels, replacing only the allocation component. At equal or shorter wall-clock time, ALLOT outperforms every compared allocation strategy with XAttention, with an 11.8 dB PSNR gain on HunyuanVideo. Extensive experiments across four additional published pipelines on Wan2.1, Wan2.2, and HunyuanVideo show that ALLOT outperforms or ties the default in all nine settings.
authors: Tianze Xia, Xiaoling Zhou, Ruya Lan, Yiqiao Liao, Chengru Song, Shiming Xiang
bullets: Full 3D attention is expensive, and different layer–step pairs have unequal effects on final-video fidelity.
ALLOT estimates each pair’s error contribution using cell probing and trajectory calibration.
It jointly optimizes sparsity densities under a measured-latency budget while retaining existing block-selection strategies and kernels.

Across five video diffusion pipelines and nine settings, ALLOT outperforms or matches the default allocation; with XAttention, it achieves an 11.8 dB PSNR gain on HunyuanVideo at equal or lower runtime.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes ALLOT, a training-free method to optimize block-sparse attention allocation in Video Diffusion Transformers, directly addressing efficiency and video generation.
papers.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.tldr: ALLOT is a training-free method that allocates block-sparse attention across layer–denoising-step pairs to improve video diffusion quality under a latency budget.

papers.abstract: The scarcity of high-quality annotated visual data remains a critical bottleneck for autonomous-driving perception. Simulators provide training data at scale, but the limited realism of synthetic videos compromises perception performance in real-world applications. To address this limitation, we propose NeuralSRender, a sim-to-real video translation framework that enhances the photorealism of synthetic videos while maintaining geometric consistency with the source scenes. Built on a pretrained video diffusion transformer (DiT), NeuralSRender uses a lightweight projector to inject geometric and material priors from G-buffers, and LoRA enables parameter-efficient adaptation. The model is trained in two stages: it first learns G-buffer conditioning from synthetic videos with accurate G-buffers, then adapts to real-world appearance using real videos with estimated G-buffers. During the second stage, an additional LoRA module is trained while the projector and first-stage LoRA remain frozen to reduce interference from estimation noise. NeuralSRender introduces only 1.45\% parameter overhead and can be trained on consumer-grade GPUs with 24 GB of memory. To support training and evaluation, we introduce GenReal, a large-scale driving video dataset comprising synthetic and real-world videos with corresponding G-buffers. Experiments demonstrate improved photorealism with competitive geometric consistency. Training perception models on our translated videos instead of raw simulator renders improves detection $\mathrm{AP}_{50}$ on nuImages from 35.1 to 40.6 and segmentation mIoU on Cityscapes from 32.4 to 40.8. Our code, data, and model weights are available at: https://github.com/WHU-USI3DV/NeuralSRender.
authors: Yipeng Lu, Youqi Liao, Zhenyu Wang, Yuning Peng, Zhen Dong
bullets: Targets the realism gap between simulator-generated videos and real-world autonomous-driving imagery.
Injects geometric and material priors through a lightweight G-buffer projector and adapts a pretrained video DiT with LoRA.
Uses two-stage training: synthetic G-buffer conditioning followed by real-world appearance adaptation with an additional LoRA module.
Introduces GenReal, a driving-video dataset containing synthetic and real videos with corresponding G-buffers.
Translated videos improve nuImages detection AP50 from 35.1 to 40.6 and Cityscapes segmentation mIoU from 32.4 to 40.8; geometric consistency remains competitive.
papers.selection_reason: G-buffer-conditioned video diffusion for sim-to-real rendering; fits video diffusion and geometric-consistency-aware video synthesis.
papers.title: NeuralSRender: G-Buffer Guided Video Diffusion for Sim-to-Real Rendering
papers.tldr: NeuralSRender uses G-buffer-guided video diffusion to make synthetic driving videos more photorealistic while preserving scene geometry, improving downstream perception performance.

papers.abstract: Reward guidance methods sample an exponential tilt of a base density using a diffusion model trained with only samples from the base distribution. Existing methods use what we call external guidance: additive terms in the drift or multiplicative terms on the transition probabilities. We propose internal guidance which leaves the output of the base denoiser unmodified and instead changes the point at which it is evaluated. For discrete distributions embedded in the hypercube $\{-1,1\}^{d}$, the denoiser of any linearly tilted density is exactly the base denoiser evaluated at a shifted and rescaled input. In practice the base denoiser is a neural network trained on noised samples of the base distribution. The required evaluation points for sampling the tilted density would be out-of-distribution for basic noising of the base distribution. We modify the training algorithm with random diagonal rescalings of the data, so that the denoiser network learns both in- and out-of-distribution evaluations of the denoiser relative to the base distribution. A single denoiser network samples binary reward tilts, class labels, and infilling with no fine-tuning and no external guidance term.
bullets: Addresses reward-guided sampling from exponential tilts using only a diffusion model trained on base-distribution samples.
Exploits an exact identity: for discrete hypercube data, the denoiser of a linearly tilted density equals the base denoiser at a shifted and rescaled input.
Trains the denoiser with random diagonal data rescalings so it supports the required out-of-distribution evaluation points.
A single network handles binary reward tilts, class-conditional sampling, and infilling without fine-tuning or external guidance terms.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes 'internal guidance' as a sampling method for tilted diffusion models. This technique modifies the evaluation point of the denoiser, relevant to diffusion-based video generation and sampling.
papers.title: Internal Guidance as a Sampling Method for Tilted Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: Internal guidance samples tilted binary diffusion distributions by evaluating one base denoiser at shifted, rescaled inputs instead of modifying its output or diffusion transitions.

papers.abstract: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. We present SolarRenderer, a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway of the backbone at the positions of the frames they describe, without a type identifier and described only in plain text, so that a single control LoRA follows arbitrary structural representations. Starting from a pretrained four-step LoRA, structure-guided distribution matching renders in four steps, 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling, while preserving the learned control. A block-causal variant extends the same design to streaming and renders 768p video in real time. To train the model, we build a frame-aligned corpus of 136K clips from game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos. Experiments on an in-distribution test set and a generalization benchmark of 16 structural representations show that SolarRenderer achieves state-of-the-art results across both, and generalizes to 11 unseen representations, including pose skeletons, drawings, and point clouds.
authors: Guian Fang, Shengju Qian, Dongyue Lu, Junchao Huang, Lutao Jiang, Xin Wang, Yiren Song, Li Jiang, Mike Zheng Shou
bullets: Addresses renderers that are engine-specific, slow, and trained with misaligned conditions.
Adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone using two lightweight LoRAs and a shared native reference pathway for arbitrary structural inputs.
Uses structure-guided distribution matching to render in four steps, reported as 12.3× faster than 50-step sampling.
A block-causal variant supports real-time 768p video streaming.
Trained on 136K frame-aligned clips; achieves state-of-the-art results on in-distribution and generalization benchmarks, including 11 unseen representations.
papers.selection_reason: Few-step structure-conditioned video rendering with diffusion LoRA adaptation.
papers.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
papers.tldr: SolarRenderer is a few-step, structure-conditioned video renderer that turns diverse coarse scene specifications into realistic video, including real-time 768p streaming.

papers.abstract: Long-horizon video generation requires retaining an ever-expanding history, but conditioning on its growing token sequence is costly. Existing methods restrict or compress historical context, potentially losing information needed for future generation. This work proposes ReCam, which groups local spatiotemporal blocks of historical latents into vectors and projects them directly into the high-dimensional hidden space of a Diffusion Transformer. The model learns to use the resulting memory tokens through native self-attention, reducing token count while retaining block-level access to the full history. To mitigate temporal drift during autoregressive rollout, we further introduce dual-pointer denoising with separate noise schedules for recent context and target frames. Among the evaluated methods, ReCam achieves the highest VBench-Long overall score of 80.1 and competitive static-scene revisitation performance on R2M-Bench. It also leads on all four consistency metrics for off-screen subject reappearance, including clothing consistency of 4.09 versus 3.03 for the best baseline.
authors: Yukuo Ma, Cong Liu, Junke Wang, Junqi Liu, Haibin Huang, Zuxuan Wu, Xuelong Li
bullets: Addresses the cost and information loss of conditioning on growing video histories.
Groups local spatiotemporal latent blocks into vectors and projects them into a Diffusion Transformer’s hidden space.
Uses native self-attention for block-level access to the full history with fewer tokens.
Introduces separate noise schedules for recent context and target frames to improve autoregressive stability.
Achieves the top reported VBench-Long score (80.1) and leads all four off-screen subject reappearance consistency metrics.
papers.selection_reason: Diffusion Transformer long-video generation with memory tokens and dual-pointer denoising.
papers.title: Recast the Past: Stable Long Video Generation with Full Context Memory
papers.tldr: ReCam enables stable long-video generation by compressing full historical context into memory tokens and using dual-pointer denoising to reduce temporal drift.

papers.abstract: Egocentric action transfer aims to decouple the semantic action from egocentric observations and reproduce them in new visual contexts, enabling scalable world simulation, embodied policy learning, and robotic data generation. Existing approaches to transferring actions rely on condition-guided video generation, which converts the observation video into explicit geometric controls (e.g., hand poses or meshes) to drive synthesis. However, these methods introduce geometric estimation errors, making it difficult to preserve physically plausible interactions when transferred to new scenes. Alternatively, motion transfer methods directly extract motion patterns from the observation video, yet motion-level features alone cannot encode rich contact dynamics, frequently leading to severe hand structural collapse and implausible contact layout. To address both limitations, we present EgoACT, a test-time framework for egocentric action transfer that operates directly on the denoising process of video diffusion models without requiring additional geometric estimators. EgoACT uses Velocity-guided Structure Anchoring to stabilize reference-consistent hand-object structure in the early denoising stage, and Sparse Correspondence Calibration to refine reliable local correspondences in the mid-to-late denoising stages. Together, these two components preserve transferable action semantics while improving temporal coherence and interaction realism. We further establish EgoActionBench, a benchmark for evaluating action preservation, visual quality, and hand-object plausibility across diverse egocentric manipulation scenarios. Experiments show that EgoACT generates more coherent and physically plausible interaction videos than strong baselines.
authors: Yue Ma, Pengjie Song, Xinyu Wang, Yi He, Zeqian Long, Fangneng Zhan, Kaichen Zhou, Hongyu Liu, Hongfa Wang, Peihao Li, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Qifeng Chen
bullets: Existing condition-guided methods suffer from geometric estimation errors, while motion-only transfer often loses contact dynamics and causes hand collapse.
EgoACT is a test-time framework that operates directly during video-diffusion denoising.
Velocity-guided Structure Anchoring stabilizes hand–object structure early in denoising.
Sparse Correspondence Calibration refines reliable local correspondences in later denoising stages.
EgoActionBench evaluates action preservation, visual quality, and hand–object plausibility; experiments report more coherent and physically plausible videos than strong baselines.
papers.selection_reason: Egocentric action transfer via video diffusion for world simulation and embodied data generation; fits interactive world models, video diffusion, and learning from human video.
papers.title: Decoupling Action from Egocentric Observation for World Simulation
papers.tldr: EgoACT transfers egocentric actions to new visual contexts by guiding video diffusion directly, preserving realistic hand–object interactions without geometric estimators.

papers.abstract: Latent diffusion models have recently achieved remarkable progress in Real-world Image Super-Resolution (Real-SR). However, existing methods consistently exhibit a persistent seesaw effect: enhancing perceptual realism compromises structural fidelity. This effect, we argue, is not intrinsic to diffusion models, but largely stems from the architectural constraints of prevailing two-stage frameworks. To address this challenge, we propose PixelSR, a novel single-stage Pixel Diffusion Transformer for Real-SR that operates directly in pixel space. Specifically, PixelSR consists of two core designs: Pixel-space Conditional Diffusion and Orthogonal Flow Decoupling. The former establishes an effective pixel-space restoration framework by integrating spatially aligned LR conditioning, visual semantic guidance, and lightweight texture refinement, thereby bypassing VAE compression and enabling end-to-end optimization directly in RGB space. Complementarily, the latter decomposes the asymmetric flow target into a low-rank semantic component and a noise-free orthogonal texture component. By routing these components to specialized branches, it achieves decoupled optimization with reduced mutual interference. Benefiting from these designs, our PixelSR restores perceptually realistic details while faithfully preserving structural content. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that PixelSR not only achieves competitive performance, but also effectively mitigates the fidelity--realism seesaw effect.
authors: Xiang Lv, Kai Zhao, Qiang Wang, Qiao Mo, Chao Zhou, Mingwen Shao
bullets: Targets the realism–fidelity trade-off attributed to architectural limitations in two-stage diffusion frameworks.
Uses pixel-space conditional diffusion with aligned low-resolution conditioning, semantic guidance, and lightweight texture refinement.
Introduces Orthogonal Flow Decoupling to separate low-rank semantic and orthogonal texture components into specialized branches.
Avoids VAE compression and enables end-to-end optimization directly in RGB space.
Experiments across multiple benchmarks show competitive performance and mitigation of the fidelity–realism seesaw effect.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a pixel-space diffusion transformer and orthogonal flow decoupling for super-resolution, offering a novel approach to diffusion efficiency and architecture.
papers.title: PixelSR: Pixel-Space Orthogonal Flow Decoupling for Real-World Image Super-Resolution
papers.tldr: PixelSR is a single-stage pixel-space diffusion transformer designed to improve Real-SR perceptual detail without sacrificing structural fidelity.

papers.abstract: Rapid advances in diffusion models have raised concerns about privacy, harmful content, and copyright violations. Concept erasure methods aim to address these risks by removing undesirable concepts from pretrained models without full retraining. However, existing approaches often degrade non-target generation quality through heuristic strength scaling (e.g., classifier-free guidance or negative prompt scaling), leading to uncontrolled and excessive semantic drift. To address this, we propose Push-Pull Attentional Anchoring (PPAA), a mechanism in the cross-attention space that displaces target representations while anchoring the scale of erasure via bounded cosine-similarity constraints. By using a relative similarity ratio instead of an absolute difference, our adaptive threshold represents a meaningful percentage of semantic retention, facilitating a single value to be applied uniformly across layers. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple concept categories, including celebrities, artistic styles, nudity, and intellectual property. Our method achieves favorable trade-offs against prior approaches on Stable Diffusion v1.4 and demonstrates its applicability to modern architectures such as FLUX.
authors: Nattanat Chatthee, Tagon Sompong, Ekapol Chuangsuwanich, Supasorn Suwajanakorn
bullets: Addresses semantic drift caused by heuristic erasure-strength scaling in existing concept-erasure methods.
Operates in cross-attention space, displacing target representations while constraining their cosine similarity.
Uses a bounded relative similarity ratio to express semantic retention and apply one adaptive threshold across layers.
Evaluated on celebrities, artistic styles, nudity, and intellectual property concepts.
Reports favorable trade-offs on Stable Diffusion v1.4 and applicability to FLUX.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a mechanism for concept erasure in diffusion models using attentional anchoring, relevant to video diffusion and multimodal model safety.
papers.title: Push-Pull Attentional Anchoring for Diffusion Concept Erasure
papers.tldr: PPAA erases unwanted concepts from diffusion models by pushing target representations away while anchoring semantic retention to reduce unintended quality loss.

papers.abstract: Diffusion-based video matting has recently emerged as a leading approach, leveraging video diffusion priors from internet-scale pretraining to achieve strong zero-shot generalization from limited synthetic data. However, the heavy compute of these diffusion backbones limits inference to a short chunk of just 6 to 24 frames, so even ordinary videos span multiple chunks. Because each chunk is matted independently from coarse mask guidance, existing methods fail to maintain consistency across chunk boundaries, producing flickering edges and discontinuous transparency. We address this with a mask-guided diffusion-matting framework built on two ideas. The RGB and mask conditioning are represented as separate token streams that interact through full spatio-temporal self-attention, letting the model adaptively combine fine RGB texture with coarse mask layout rather than committing to a fixed channel-wise fusion. On top of this, we propose a novel pair of learnable embeddings, the preserve token and the refine token, that act as a per-frame conditioning interface and enable a sliding-window inference scheme in which already-generated mattes are propagated across chunk boundaries for local temporal consistency, complemented by a globally shared reference anchor at every chunk to prevent error accumulation in long sequences without any additional training. Across standard video matting benchmarks and in-the-wild long footage, our framework outperforms prior diffusion-based methods in both fine-detail accuracy and temporal consistency, and uniquely maintains consistency across chunk boundaries on long videos.
authors: Sangbeom Lim, Seoung Wug Oh, Heeji Yoon, Seungryong Kim, Joon-Young Lee
bullets: Addresses flickering edges and discontinuous transparency caused by independently processing short video chunks.
Uses separate RGB and mask token streams with full spatio-temporal attention for adaptive conditioning.
Introduces learnable preserve and refine tokens to propagate previous mattes during sliding-window inference.
Adds a shared reference anchor to maintain global consistency and limit error accumulation without extra training.
Outperforms prior diffusion-based methods in fine-detail accuracy and temporal consistency, including on long in-the-wild videos.
papers.selection_reason: Diffusion-based video matting with token-based temporal consistency; transferable to video diffusion and editing.
papers.title: VideoMaMa++: Temporally Consistent Video Matting via Preserve-and-Refine Token
papers.tldr: VideoMaMa++ improves long-video diffusion matting by preserving and refining masks across chunk boundaries for sharper, more temporally consistent results.

papers.abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models can produce unsafe content, while output filtering intervenes only after synthesis. We investigate whether native generation signals enable early detection of unsafe and adversarial inputs. We find that classifier-free guidance exposes strong safety signals in conditional responses, accessible through compact statistics and linear readouts. Based on this finding, we propose Conditional Semantic Trajectory Interception (CSTI), which aggregates activation contrasts between conditional and unconditional responses at early checkpoints for calibrated risk detection. CSTI fits concept-specific detectors using canonical concept and safe examples, without attack samples, intermediate image decoding, or generator modification. Across five generators, four adversarial attack collections, and two general NSFW datasets, CSTI achieves the strongest overall performance among six baselines at a matched 5% FPR. Early interception reduces generation latency by over 60% on intercepted paths. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of native conditional responses for early safety interception.
authors: Yanchun Li, Yujin Wu, Gangkai Shen, Ming Yang, Li Zeng, Xianlong Wang, Hangtao Zhang, Shujuan Tian
bullets: Addresses the limitation of output filtering, which acts only after unsafe content is synthesized.
Uses contrasts between conditional and unconditional responses at early diffusion checkpoints with compact statistics and linear readouts.
Trains concept-specific detectors from canonical concept and safe examples, without attack samples.
Across five generators, four attack collections, and two NSFW datasets, it had the strongest overall performance among six baselines at 5% FPR.
Intercepting unsafe generations early reduced latency by over 60% on intercepted paths.
papers.selection_reason: Investigates early interception of unsafe inputs in text-to-image generation using native generation signals. This contributes to safety mechanisms in diffusion models and reduces generation latency.
papers.title: When Guidance Becomes a Guard: Early Interception of Unsafe Inputs in Text-to-Image Generation
papers.tldr: CSTI detects unsafe or adversarial text-to-image inputs early by analyzing classifier-free guidance signals, avoiding image decoding and generator changes.

papers.abstract: Diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos but remain computationally expensive. Sparse attention and temporal caching reduce computation within and across denoising steps, respectively, offering a natural composition. However, predictions produced with sparse attention become sources for temporal reuse, coupling their errors along the sampling trajectory. We observe that improving the accuracy of these sources recovers fidelity without changing the reuse schedule, and that sparsification errors remain directionally aligned across nearby steps, suggesting that correction information can be shared rather than recomputed. These observations motivate RECAP, a training-free method that couples sparse attention with hierarchical caching through reciprocal correction, adaptively coordinated by online error feedback. Cached dense refinement corrects omitted interactions in current sparse estimates, while fresh sparse statistics track input changes and regulate the aging correction. The resulting predictions then renew the sources for whole-step prediction reuse, allowing prediction history to advance between dense refreshes. We evaluate RECAP on multiple video diffusion models against sparse-attention methods, caching methods, and their direct compositions. On HunyuanVideo at 720p 5-second generation, RECAP achieves a 3.05x speedup and outperforms all tested direct compositions in both fidelity and inference speed.
authors: Tiange Xu, Kai Liu, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang
bullets: Addresses the computational cost of diffusion transformers for high-quality video generation.
Uses training-free reciprocal correction: cached dense refinement fixes sparse-attention omissions, while fresh sparse statistics monitor input changes.
Employs online error feedback to coordinate sparse attention, hierarchical caching, and correction aging without changing the reuse schedule.
Evaluated across multiple video diffusion models against sparse-attention, caching, and direct-composition baselines.
On HunyuanVideo at 720p for 5-second videos, reports a 3.05× speedup and better fidelity and speed than tested direct compositions.
papers.selection_reason: Directly addresses efficient video diffusion via sparse attention and hierarchical caching, fitting both efficient AI and video diffusion interests.
papers.title: RECAP: Reciprocal Sparse Attention and Hierarchical Caching for Efficient Video Diffusion
papers.tldr: RECAP accelerates video diffusion by combining sparse attention and hierarchical caching with reciprocal error correction, achieving faster and higher-fidelity generation than direct combinations of existing methods.

papers.abstract: RGBA video generation is essential for creating compositable visual assets in filmmaking, game development, and digital content production. However, generating high-quality RGB appearance alongside temporally coherent transparency remains a significant challenge. Existing text-to-RGBA video methods often entangle RGB and alpha distributions and offer limited control over the precise appearance of a target asset. In addition, incorporating image conditioning typically suffers from the emergence-disappearance effects, which fail existing first-frame or first-and-last-frame conditions due to their fully transparent boundary frames. To address these issues, we present Wan-Alpha++, a unified framework that brings controllable RGBA video generation to both text- and image-to-video diffusion backbones through a shared RGBA latent space, extending our conference version Wan-Alpha from the text-conditioned setting to image-conditioned generation with an interior reference frame. Our method first learns shiftable RGB-alpha distributions while preserving the pretrained RGB prior. Specifically, we introduce a transparency-aware bidirectional diffusion objective to produce distinguishable RGBA latent representations, and a transparency-guided mean sampler that shifts the noise distribution to improve transparency generation and enable spatial controllability. Building upon this RGBA generation prior, we introduce temporal phase reparameterization for image-conditioned effect generation. By cyclically transforming a zero-positive-zero alpha pattern into a positive-zero-positive pattern, it relocates visible content to both temporal boundaries, facilitating effective appearance conditioning with limited RGBA data.
authors: Haotian Dong, Xin Wang, Wenjing Wang, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Yan Tina Luximon, Ping Li, Wanchao Su, Ke Xu, Di Lin
bullets: Targets entangled RGB–alpha generation and weak image-conditioning behavior at transparent video boundaries.
Uses a shared RGBA latent space across text-to-video and image-to-video diffusion backbones.
Introduces transparency-aware bidirectional diffusion and a transparency-guided mean sampler for improved and spatially controllable transparency.
Applies temporal phase reparameterization to convert zero-positive-zero alpha patterns into boundary-visible positive-zero-positive patterns for image conditioning.
Extends Wan-Alpha from text-conditioned generation to image-conditioned transparent effects using an interior reference frame.
papers.selection_reason: Controllable RGBA video generation built on diffusion backbones.
papers.title: Wan-Alpha++: Animating a Single RGBA Asset into Controllable Transparent Video Effects
papers.tldr: Wan-Alpha++ generates controllable, temporally coherent transparent RGBA videos from text or a single interior reference image.

papers.abstract: Despite achieving high visual fidelity, video models still suffer from physical hallucinations, limiting their reliability as world simulators. Existing methods leverage model-internal or external signals to improve physical plausibility, but their roles and limitations require a unified explanation. We propose a two-dimensional physical-hallucination risk framework that defines low-density sampling risk and high-density drifting risk. The first risk captures generations assigned low likelihood by the video model, for example, a ball suddenly teleporting despite the model favoring continuous motion, while the second risk captures physical inconsistencies in high-likelihood generations, for example, a ball bouncing progressively higher without additional energy. Our analysis explains how model-internal signals steer sampling toward higher-density regions of the learned distribution to address low-density sampling risk. However, higher model likelihood does not guarantee physical plausibility, motivating external guidance to address high-density drifting risk. Based on this framework, we develop Hallucination-Aware Sampler (HA-Sampler), which applies external physical guidance within latent refinement to generate physically plausible videos, and HA-Scorer, which derives a likelihood-based signal from the generator itself for evaluating generated videos using continuous normalizing flow (CNF), with coarse ODE integration and finite-difference divergence estimates. Experiments on Physics-IQ and VideoPhy benchmarks support our theoretical analysis and demonstrate that our methods outperform the compared sampling and scoring SOTA baselines.
authors: Chenyan Zheng, Fan Wu, Ruibo Li, Jiaxing Li, Minghao Yang, Bang Zhang, Guosheng Lin
bullets: Defines low-density sampling risk as unlikely events and high-density drifting risk as physically inconsistent but likely generations.
Explains that model-internal likelihood signals can reduce low-density errors but cannot ensure physical plausibility.
Introduces HA-Sampler, which applies external physical guidance during latent refinement.
Introduces HA-Scorer, a generator-based likelihood signal using continuous normalizing flows for video evaluation.
Experiments on Physics-IQ and VideoPhy support the analysis and report better performance than compared SOTA baselines.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes Hallucination-Aware Sampler (HA-Sampler) to address physical hallucinations in video generation. Relevant to video world models and video diffusion.
papers.title: Risk Decomposition for Hallucination-Aware Video Sampling
papers.tldr: The paper decomposes physical hallucinations in video generation into low-density sampling errors and high-density physical drift, then introduces tools to mitigate and evaluate both.

papers.abstract: Diffusion models primarily rely on general-purpose ODE-based numerical methods for training-free accelerated sampling, but performance degrades with coarse time discretization. In this paper, we propose optimal linear leaps (LEAP), a specialized method grounded in theoretical and empirical investigations of sampling trajectory geometry. Built upon low-dimensionality and cross-trajectory consistency, LEAP formulates a supervised least-squares optimization problem within the local trajectory subspace, achieving a precise approximation of future states without model evaluations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LEAP outperforms previous methods across diverse modalities, including text-to-image (Stable Diffusion 3.5, FLUX.1-dev) and image-to-3D (TRELLIS.2) generation. Furthermore, LEAP can be seamlessly integrated into existing solver-based methods, offering a plug-and-play enhancement for modern diffusion models. Code is available at https://github.com/zju-pi/LEAP.
authors: Haowei Zheng, Zhenyu Zhou, Jiawei Chen, Can Wang, Defang Chen
bullets: Addresses performance degradation caused by coarse time discretization in accelerated diffusion sampling.
Uses low-dimensionality and cross-trajectory consistency to formulate a supervised least-squares optimization problem.
Approximates future sampling states without additional model evaluations.
Works across text-to-image and image-to-3D generation, including Stable Diffusion 3.5, FLUX.1-dev, and TRELLIS.2.
Can be integrated as a plug-and-play enhancement with existing solver-based methods.
papers.selection_reason: Accelerates ODE-based diffusion sampling with optimal linear leaps (LEAP). This improves inference efficiency for diffusion models, relevant to efficient AI and video diffusion.
papers.title: LEAP: Accelerating ODE-based Diffusion Sampling with Optimal Linear Leaps
papers.tldr: LEAP accelerates ODE-based diffusion sampling by predicting future states through optimal linear extrapolation in a local trajectory subspace, reducing the need for model evaluations.

papers.abstract: Zero-shot diffusion image compression based on reverse channel coding achieves high perceptual quality at low bitrates without retraining, yet its bitstream remains vulnerable to bit flips. Prior work has shown that a joint combinatorial representation can amplify a single bit flip into substitutions of multiple atoms and that indexing each atom independently confines this error propagation. However, independent indexing reduces the number of atoms that fit within the bit budget and gives the decoder no indication of which atoms are corrupted. To address these issues, we propose BitFlat, a training-free error-localizing bitstream framework with two components. Blockwise Locality Alignment (BLA) decomposes the globally coupled atom selection at each diffusion step into independent selection units, each describing one signed atom from a dedicated codebook with a fixed-width field, so that any bit error affects only the unit in which it occurs. Reliability-Aware Diffusion Control (RADC) uses the bits saved by BLA to impose structured valid-codeword constraints within each field and converts the decoding state of each field into a binary reliability gate, which turns detected corrupted atoms into erasures at known positions and excludes them from noise synthesis. BitFlat requires neither target residuals nor additional network forward passes and leaves the diffusion model unchanged. Experiments on Kodak, DIV2K, and CLIC2020 show that BitFlat outperforms conventional, learned, and diffusion-based codecs at bit error rates from $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-2}$ and, even with $26.7\%$ fewer bits, surpasses Robust Turbo-DDCM.
authors: Xinfeng Deng, Li Zhou, Haitao Chen, Shengjie Wu, Lingjin Kong, Nan Li, Haitao Zhao, Dongtang Ma
bullets: Addresses bit-flip vulnerability in reverse-channel-coding diffusion compression at low bitrates.
Blockwise Locality Alignment isolates each signed atom in an independent fixed-width codeword field.
Reliability-Aware Diffusion Control detects invalid fields, gates corrupted atoms, and excludes them from noise synthesis.
Training-free: requires no target residuals, extra network forward passes, or diffusion-model changes.
Outperforms conventional, learned, and diffusion codecs across tested bit-error rates, and surpasses Robust Turbo-DDCM with 26.7% fewer bits.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes BitFlat, a training-free error-localizing bitstream framework for robust diffusion image compression, addressing error propagation in the bitstream.
papers.title: BitFlat: Error-Localized Bitstream Design for Robust Diffusion Image Compression
papers.tldr: BitFlat makes zero-shot diffusion image compression resilient to bit flips by localizing errors and turning detected corruptions into erasures during decoding.

papers.abstract: Video generation models produce visually compelling motion but systematically fail on fluid phenomena, including smoke, fire, and explosion debris, where outputs lack coherent vortical structure and collapse to bland dynamics that violate the physics of real fluids. Classical solvers achieve high physical fidelity but require detailed 3D scenes and carefully tuned parameters, making them impractical for in-the-wild imagery and video generation. We address this gap by injecting a data-driven fluid prior into a pre-trained video model, trained on a mixture of high-fidelity Houdini simulation data with paired velocity-field ground truth and curated in-the-wild fluid video data for appearance diversity. The core of our approach is a dual stream architecture that predicts per-frame velocity fields alongside RGB, supervised by simulation ground truth. This auxiliary signal regularizes generation toward physically consistent motion and exposes an interpretable physical quantity that we further leverage as a reward for velocity-aware direct preference optimization. Our model produces substantially more realistic fluid dynamics sequences than strong video baselines and optimization-based methods. Project page: https://y-zheng18.github.io/FluidGen/
authors: Yang Zheng, Zizhang Li, Boyang Deng, Jan Ackermann, Lei Shu, Yinghao Xu, Jiajun Wu, Gordon Wetzstein, Leonidas Guibas
bullets: Targets fluid videos whose generated motion often lacks coherent vortices and physically plausible dynamics.
Combines high-fidelity simulated fluids with in-the-wild videos to provide both physical supervision and visual diversity.
Uses a dual-stream model that predicts RGB frames and per-frame velocity fields.
Further applies velocity-aware direct preference optimization using the predicted physical signal as a reward.
The authors report more realistic fluid dynamics than strong video baselines and optimization-based methods.
papers.selection_reason: Generates physically consistent fluid dynamics by injecting a data-driven fluid prior and supervising velocity fields, addressing a failure mode in standard video generation models.
papers.title: FluidGen: Physics-Aware Fluid Video Generation via Motion-Guided Post-Training
papers.tldr: FluidGen improves video generation of smoke, fire, and debris by guiding a pretrained model with learned velocity fields and physics-aware preference optimization.

papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models generate streaming video of arbitrary length by conditioning each new chunk of frames on those already generated. However, they suffer from exposure bias, where a model trained on clean context must continue from its own imperfect outputs, and errors compound until quality collapses within seconds (drift). Existing methods either require cluster-scale base retraining, apply training-free inference corrections with inconsistent results, or train frozen-base correctors for sampling and cache errors. We instead find that drift is largely deterministic and therefore learnable, as holding the noisy state fixed while varying only the history reveals a counterfactual velocity gap that is ~95% systematic across noise seeds. Based on this observation, we introduce Clean Forcing, which trains a 5.9M-parameter LoRA corrector on the frozen base model to regress this gap, with a closed-loop stage that adds DAgger-style aggregation and a drift-contraction objective to expose the corrector to its own rollouts. Because the clean histories can be the base model's own single-shot generations, training needs no real videos, and the merged corrector adds no inference cost. In 50 s text-to-video generation, Clean Forcing reduces {\Delta}-drift from +11.3 to +1.65 without real video and to -0.16 with 40 real clips, improving on the best published result of +3.57 with over 150x less data. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Clean Forcing outperforms prior methods in aesthetic quality and data efficiency with reduced drift for long-horizon video generation.
authors: Wenqing Wang, Joonghyuk Shin, Jonathan Tremblay, Chan Hee Song, Yun Fu
bullets: Addresses exposure bias and compounding errors that cause streaming video quality to collapse over time.
Learns a counterfactual velocity gap shown to be largely deterministic across noise seeds.
Trains a 5.9M-parameter LoRA corrector using closed-loop, DAgger-style rollout aggregation and drift-contraction training.
Requires no real videos when using the frozen base model’s own single-shot generations, and adds no inference cost after merging.
In 50-second generation, reduces Δ-drift from +11.3 to +1.65 without real video and to −0.16 with 40 real clips, outperforming prior reported results with far less data.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses the drift problem in autoregressive video diffusion models by training a small corrector on a frozen base, improving long-horizon generation stability.
papers.title: Clean Forcing: Drift-Resistant Autoregressive Video Diffusion with a Frozen Base
papers.tldr: Clean Forcing stabilizes long-horizon autoregressive video diffusion by learning and correcting systematic drift with a lightweight LoRA adapter while keeping the base model frozen.

papers.abstract: Language-guided video generation often captures scene content while missing the requested motion. We present ViMoLa (Video Motion Language), which predicts a motion prior from language and injects it into a frozen image-to-video backbone. A spatial vector-quantized autoencoder compresses dense trajectories into 64 tokens from a 512-entry codebook; a 28M-parameter transformer predicts the tokens from text; and zero-gated cross-attention adapters condition every frozen Wan~2.2 DiT block through forward hooks. Trained on 462K videos from Something-Something~v2 and Kinetics-400, ViMoLa raises directional accuracy from 0.287 to 0.442 (chance 0.250), with similar measured generative quality. Across-prompt shuffled codes achieve 0.283, supporting the importance of prompt-matched token content. A low-rank adapter reaches 0.428 at 1.45% additional forward-pass FLOPs, and reusing the tokenizer and language model with newly trained CogVideoX adapters raises accuracy from 0.301 to 0.398.
