Control remains imperfect: oracle codes reach 0.531, compound-motion gains are smaller, and the adapter does not explicitly preserve token-to-patch assignments.
bullets: Targets the common failure of videos to follow requested motion despite matching scene content.
Compresses dense trajectories into 64 discrete tokens and predicts them from language with a 28M-parameter transformer.
Uses zero-gated cross-attention adapters to condition frozen Wan 2.2 DiT blocks; a low-rank variant adds 1.45% forward-pass FLOPs.
Raises directional accuracy from 0.287 to 0.442, with similar measured generative quality; shuffled motion codes provide little benefit.
Control remains imperfect: oracle codes reach 0.531, compound motions improve less, and token-to-patch assignments are not explicitly preserved.
papers.selection_reason: Discrete motion tokens for language-guided video generation; fits video diffusion and multimodal conditioning.
papers.title: ViMoLa: Discrete Motion Tokens for Language-Guided Video Generation
papers.tldr: ViMoLa improves language-guided video motion by predicting discrete motion tokens from text and injecting them into a frozen image-to-video model.

papers.abstract: Existing motion transfer methods excel at exact, rigid motion replication from reference videos to target scenes, whereas they often fail to account for the compatibility between the transferred motion and the target scene environment in accordance with physical laws. In this work, we propose MotionShift, a novel motion transfer framework that achieves high-fidelity motion transfer while ensuring physical compatibility with the target scene. In particular, we design a planner--evaluator iterative motion adaptation mechanism, in which a Large Language Model (LLM) acts as the planner to generate motion trajectories by leveraging its strong semantic reasoning capabilities, while a Vision-Language Model (VLM) serves as the evaluator to rectify the motion based on its superior visual perception and scene understanding. Through this planner--evaluator synergistic reasoning process, the motion is adapted to the target scene in a training-free manner. The adapted motion is then used as a generative condition for an image-to-video (I2V) model to render videos in the target scene. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MotionShift achieves high-fidelity and physically compatible motion transfer across diverse and complex scenes. Moreover, we show that MotionShift can be readily integrated into existing trajectory-conditioned I2V models, endowing them with realistic motion transfer capabilities.
authors: Yanchen Liu, Junyao Gao, Yanan Sun, Wensheng Chen, Guangming Lu, Wenjie Pei
bullets: Addresses the lack of physical and environmental compatibility in existing reference-video motion transfer methods.
Uses an LLM planner to generate motion trajectories and a VLM evaluator to visually assess and rectify them.
Iteratively adapts motion to the target scene without additional training.
Feeds the adapted motion as conditioning to an image-to-video model for target-scene rendering.
Experiments report realistic, physically compatible transfer across diverse complex scenes and integration with existing trajectory-conditioned I2V models.
papers.selection_reason: LLM/VLM planner-evaluator motion transfer for image-to-video generation, enabling physically compatible motion in target scenes.
papers.title: MotionShift: Environment-Compatible Motion Transfer via Planner-Evaluator Synergistic Adaptation
papers.tldr: MotionShift enables high-fidelity motion transfer that adapts to target-scene constraints through training-free planner–evaluator reasoning.

papers.abstract: Synthesizing a monocular video from a new camera trajectory requires preserving the observed scene geometry and motion while completing regions that become newly visible. Feed-forward 4D reconstructors recover the structure of the observed scene, whereas video diffusion models provide a generative prior for completing unseen content. We introduce Holo4D, a video reshooting framework that uses reconstructed 3D trajectories as a holistic source-view 4D scaffold. We project these trajectories into the requested views and encode their geometry and source appearance to guide a pretrained video diffusion model. Together with the source video and target cameras, the scaffold grounds generation in reconstructed observations while leaving unsupported regions to the generative prior. Experiments demonstrate the value of trajectory-based conditioning for camera control and novel-view synthesis. The framework accommodates different 4D reconstructors without retraining the video generator, allowing it to benefit from future advances in source reconstruction. More details can be found in our project page.
authors: Yushi Lan, Zeren Jiang, Koichi Namekata, Xingang Pan, Chuanxia Zheng, Andrea Vedaldi
bullets: Addresses monocular video synthesis along new camera trajectories with newly visible content.
Builds a holistic 4D scaffold from reconstructed 3D scene trajectories and motion.
Projects scaffold geometry and source appearance into target views to condition a pretrained video diffusion model.
Uses source video and target cameras to ground generation in observations while delegating unsupported regions to the generative prior.
Experiments show trajectory-based conditioning improves camera control and novel-view synthesis; the generator requires no retraining for different reconstructors.
papers.selection_reason: Uses holistic 4D reconstruction as geometric control for video diffusion reshooting, advancing novel-view video synthesis.
papers.title: Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion
papers.tldr: Holo4D combines feed-forward 4D reconstruction with video diffusion to generate novel-camera videos while preserving observed geometry and plausibly completing unseen regions.

papers.abstract: Camera-conditioned video diffusion models often suffer from inaccurate camera control and geometric inconsisten- cies because camera constraints and estimated geometry are only weakly enforced during denoising. Existing reme- dies often require costly geometry-aware fine-tuning or ad- ditional 3D supervision. We introduce GeoART, a training- free self-refinement framework that improves camera con- trollability through geometry-aware test-time scaling. At selected denoising steps, GeoART generates multiple can- didates within the Predict-and-Perturb cycle and eval- uates them using a geometry prior, without directly modify- ing the denoising trajectory. A confidence gate suppresses unreliable geometric evidence, while rank-calibrated prob- abilistic selection combines score magnitude and relative rank to choose the next refinement state. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in camera controlla- bility, multi-view consistency, and visual quality over exist- ing sampling and self-refinement methods, without training or modifying the pretrained video diffusion model
bullets: Addresses weak enforcement of camera constraints and estimated geometry during denoising.
Generates and evaluates multiple candidates at selected denoising steps within a Predict-and-Perturb cycle.
Uses a confidence gate to suppress unreliable geometry signals.
Applies rank-calibrated probabilistic selection to combine score magnitude and relative rank.
Reported experiments show consistent gains in camera controllability, multi-view consistency, and visual quality without modifying or retraining the pretrained model.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free geometry-aware test-time refinement for camera-conditioned video diffusion, improving controllability and consistency.
papers.title: GeoART: Geometry-Aware Refinement via Test-Time Scaling for Camera-Conditioned Video Diffusion
papers.tldr: GeoART improves camera control and geometric consistency in camera-conditioned video diffusion through training-free, geometry-aware test-time refinement.

papers.abstract: Novel view synthesis under trajectory changes is essential for autonomous driving simulation, yet existing methods struggle to generate consistent videos when extrapolating to unseen viewpoints such as lane shifts. Reconstruction-based approaches maintain geometric consistency but degrade in visual quality under large viewpoint changes, while reconstruct-then-restore methods often produce visually plausible frames yet suffer from geometric and temporal inconsistencies. We present GeoV2V, a geometry-grounded video-to-video diffusion framework that synthesizes temporally coherent driving videos along novel trajectories by integrating LiDAR and depth-derived geometric priors with full-video conditioning in the Wan 2.1 backbone. A key challenge in learning cross-lane transformations is the lack of synchronized multi-trajectory supervision in real-world datasets. To address this, we also introduce Para4D, a synthetic dataset capturing synchronized multi-lane driving videos within dynamic scenes, which provides explicit supervision for lane-shift generation and serves as a strong training prior for geometry-consistent view synthesis. Experiments on Waymo, nuScenes, and Para4D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in visual quality, geometric consistency, and robustness to complex lighting dynamics under large trajectory shifts. Project page: https://xiyuche.github.io/GeoV2V/
authors: Yuchen Xi, Yuhan Guo, Chenwei Hou, Zixu Liu, Jin Fang, Jason Liu, Ruigang Yang
bullets: Targets novel-view synthesis for autonomous-driving simulation under large trajectory changes.
Uses LiDAR- and depth-derived geometric priors with full-video conditioning in the Wan 2.1 video diffusion backbone.
Introduces Para4D, a synthetic dataset with synchronized multi-lane driving videos for explicit lane-shift supervision.
Evaluations on Waymo, nuScenes, and Para4D show strong visual quality, geometric consistency, and robustness to complex lighting dynamics.
Scope: the method addresses trajectory extrapolation, especially cross-lane transformations, where real-world synchronized supervision is limited.
papers.selection_reason: Geometry-grounded video diffusion for driving scene generation along novel trajectories, directly fitting video diffusion and world-model-adjacent generation.
papers.title: GeoV2V: Geometry-Grounded Video Diffusion Model for Driving Scene Generation
papers.tldr: GeoV2V combines geometric priors and full-video diffusion conditioning to generate temporally coherent, geometry-consistent driving videos along unseen trajectories such as lane shifts.

papers.abstract: Video generation models synthesize visual sequences from text and image inputs. Extending video generation to long animations requires actions, dialogue, camera coverage, and narrative developments to remain coordinated across scenes. Executable scene programs make these decisions available for inspection. Constructing an entire story before observing its execution can leave later scenes dependent on unrealized events. We present SpriteStage, a progressive scene programming framework that builds animation through iterative enactment and engine reorchestration. Iterative enactment generates each scene from an accepted world checkpoint and narrative snapshot, executes it on a shared spatial stage, and uses runtime and visual feedback to revise the relevant actions or story beats. The accepted outcome becomes the starting state for the next scene. Engine reorchestration maps the resulting draft to production assets and engine capabilities while retaining its events, geometry, and timing. Inspection of the assembled sequence and frozen replay carry the accepted performance into the final video. Three complete animations, ranging from approximately 9.9 to 14.3 minutes, demonstrate the framework's effectiveness in producing extended narratives through scene programming and engine execution.
authors: Zhaoqi Wang, Zijian Zhang, Jiamou Liu
bullets: Targets the coordination of actions, dialogue, camera coverage, and narrative developments across long animations.
Builds each scene from an accepted world checkpoint and narrative snapshot, then uses runtime and visual feedback for revision.
Reorchestrates scene drafts onto production assets and engine capabilities while preserving events, geometry, and timing.
Uses sequence inspection and frozen replay to transfer accepted performances into the final video.
Demonstrated through three complete animations lasting approximately 9.9–14.3 minutes.
papers.selection_reason: Directly addresses long-horizon animation generation, a core challenge in video generation and world models. The framework of progressive scene programming and engine reorchestration is technically relevant to video synthesis and predictive modeling.
papers.title: SpriteStage: Long Horizon Animation Generation via Progressive Scene Programming and Replay
papers.tldr: SpriteStage generates long-form animations by progressively scripting, executing, inspecting, and revising scenes while carrying accepted world states forward.

papers.abstract: Unified audio-video creation requires a single model capable of text-conditioned joint synthesis, bidirectional cross-modal generation, and instruction-guided editing across both modalities. Existing methods rely heavily on paired corpora, which are scarce for joint generation and even rarer for editing. Consequently, they are spent learning single-branch generative and editing capabilities that abundant unimodal data could readily teach, rather than on the cross-modal coupling. Furthermore, prevailing systems apply a single shared noise schedule to both modalities, neglecting two critical limitations. First, due to the significant discrepancy in information density, video requires prolonged high noise to organize spatial and motion structure, whereas the sparser audio signal can settle earlier during the synthesis process, the dynamics a uniform schedule might compromise. Second, lockstep denoising leaves asymmetric workflows, such as conditioning on one modality to synthesize or edit another, untrained. We present UniAVC, which addresses both obstacles. It first trains each branch on unimodal dataset to full generative and editing competence, and subsequently dedicates paired data to exploit cross-modal correspondence. Modality-decoupled schedulers meanwhile warp the noise schedule independently from a shared timestep, while subtasks with one clean modality directly supervise asymmetric configurations. These settings respectively enable intent-aware editing, which preserves one modality intact while enlisting it to constrain the other, and post-inference self-refinement, which regenerates only an unsatisfactory branch against an accepted one. UniAVC thus spans multiple creation tasks from a single set of weights without task-specific adapters.
authors: Kien T. Pham, Yuhao Liu, Chong Hou Choi, Zhenqi He, Yanghao Wang, Chenyang Lei, Rui Liu, Qifeng Chen, Long Chen
bullets: Addresses scarce paired audio-video data by first training audio and video branches on abundant unimodal data, then using paired data for cross-modal learning.
Uses independently warped noise schedules so video can denoise longer while audio settles earlier.
Trains asymmetric workflows where one clean modality guides synthesis or editing of the other.
Supports intent-aware editing that preserves one modality while modifying the other.
Enables post-inference self-refinement by regenerating only an unsatisfactory modality, without task-specific adapters.
papers.selection_reason: Unified audio-video diffusion with asymmetric noise schedules and cross-modal generation/editing fits video diffusion.
papers.title: UniAVC: Unified Audio-Video Creation via Progressive Training and Asymmetric Scheduling
papers.tldr: UniAVC enables one model to jointly create, cross-condition, and edit audio-video content by combining progressive training with modality-specific denoising schedules.

papers.abstract: Simulation-to-real driving video diffusion models can translate photorealistic scenes, but they typically represent pedestrians and cyclists, vulnerable road users (VRUs), as generic object classes. This is insufficient for vulnerable road users whose safety-relevant appearance depends on articulated pose and identity. We present BodyBridge and Grounded Body Layers (GBL), a simulator-derived, pixel-aligned representation that combines scene geometry, canonical per-pixel body correspondence, and exact VRU masks. GBL provides explicit articulation to the video diffusion model, emphasizes VRU regions during control-branch post-training, and supports additive composition with scene-geometry control at inference. It also enables per-joint evaluation of generated VRUs and a failure taxonomy for identity errors. On CARLA-to-real translation, BodyBridge improves near-range PCK@0.5 by 22% over the released depth-conditioned baseline. Replacing normal-map body control with canonical correspondence reduces body flips by 18%, while composition reduces near-range facing flips by 27%. These results show that explicit body grounding complements scene-level control and improves pose-faithful VRU generation. All code, data, and model checkpoints will be made publicly available to support reproducible, pedestrian-aware autonomous driving research.
bullets: Addresses the limits of generic VRU representations, whose articulated pose and identity are safety-relevant.
Introduces Grounded Body Layers (GBL): simulator-derived, pixel-aligned body correspondence, scene geometry, and exact VRU masks.
Uses VRU-focused control-branch post-training and additive composition with scene-geometry control at inference.
On CARLA-to-real translation, improves near-range PCK@0.5 by 22% over a released depth-conditioned baseline.
Canonical correspondence and composition reduce body flips by 18% and near-range facing flips by 27%, respectively.
papers.selection_reason: Sim-to-real driving video diffusion with articulated body grounding for pedestrians and cyclists.
papers.title: BodyBridge: Grounded Body Layers for Sim-to-Real Translation of Vulnerable Road Users
papers.tldr: BodyBridge improves sim-to-real generation of pose- and identity-faithful pedestrians and cyclists by grounding video diffusion in explicit body geometry and correspondence.

papers.abstract: Sign language production (SLP) aims to synthesize expressive signing motion from written text. Modeling signing motion presents two key temporal challenges. First, fine-grained hand articulations demand higher temporal resolution than relatively slower body movements. Second, signing events unfold over variable durations, calling for adaptive temporal scheduling during generation. To address these challenges, we first introduce a Multi-Rate Vector Quantizer (MRVQ), an articulation-decoupled motion tokenizer that represents the body and both hands as separate discrete streams at distinct temporal resolutions. Building on this representation, we propose BLANC (BLock-wise Adaptive diffusioN with Articulatory Clock), a gloss-free SLP framework that generates variable-duration motion blocks causally while denoising tokens in parallel within each block. At its core, a Latent Articulatory Clock (LAC) learns temporal structure from multi-scale motion-derived partitions to predict block durations and sequence termination during generation. We further introduce inference-time body-conditioned hand refinement to improve coordination across articulators. Extensive experiments on PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily demonstrate that BLANC achieves state-of-the-art performance in sign language production.
authors: Youngmin Kim, Seoyeong Hwang, Sujung Hong, Seong Jae Hwang
bullets: Addresses the need for fine-grained hand timing and variable-duration signing events.
Uses a Multi-Rate Vector Quantizer to encode the body and both hands as separate streams at distinct temporal resolutions.
Generates variable-length motion blocks causally while denoising tokens in parallel within each block.
A Latent Articulatory Clock predicts block durations and when generation should terminate.
Body-conditioned hand refinement improves coordination; experiments on PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily report state-of-the-art performance.
papers.selection_reason: Diffusion-based variable-duration motion generation with multi-rate temporal tokenization and adaptive block-wise scheduling; technical ideas transferable to video generation and temporal world modeling.
papers.title: BLANC: Adaptive Temporal Scheduling for Sign Language Production
papers.tldr: BLANC generates expressive sign-language motion with adaptive timing and separate temporal resolutions for body and hand articulation.

papers.abstract: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real images. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID. Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/.
authors: Soumik Mukhopadhyay, Long Mai, Abhinav Shrivastava, Aniruddha Mahapatra
bullets: Pixel diffusion avoids the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder, but its prediction parameterization strongly affects performance.
MFlow learns the preferred interpolation between x₀- and u-prediction across data principal directions during diffusion training.
The preferred parameterization depends on data representation and model capacity; larger models favor velocity prediction more strongly.
Experiments on ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation show competitive or improved generative performance across settings.
Pixel diffusion transformers exhibit a persistent high-frequency deficit; post-hoc ConvRefiner addresses it with lightweight adversarial training while freezing the backbone and preserving FID.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes adaptive parameterization and a conv refiner for pixel-space diffusion transformers, with evaluations on video generation among other settings.
papers.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
papers.tldr: MFlow adaptively combines clean-image and velocity prediction for pixel-space diffusion transformers, while ConvRefiner restores missing high-frequency detail without degrading FID.

papers.abstract: Video diffusion models (VDMs) trained on internet-scale data encode a rich prior on appearance, motion, and physics that is difficult to replicate with explicit 3D rendering and costly 3D data capture. We introduce Video Diffusion Avatars (VDAs), a method that creates photo-realistic, multi-view consistent avatars from a single image by fine-tuning a VDM for precise control over camera viewpoint, facial expression, and upper-body pose. Departing from 3D morphable models (3DMMs), VDAs use a learned expression space that lifts the expressiveness ceiling of 3DMMs, e.g., for the tongue and mouth interior. However, learned expression codes exhibit heavy viewpoint bias, as our DISTRACT benchmark reveals. We show that this bias can be removed through disentanglement, enabling their use as driving signals for multi-view consistent avatars. Camera and upper-body pose are controlled jointly via proxy-mesh renderings, giving independent control over expression, pose, and viewpoint. A camera-triplet training strategy makes the approach efficient: our models train for 34 hours on a single A100 using only public multi-view data. VDAs outperform state-of-the-art single-image 3D avatars on novel-view reenactment, reducing face LPIPS by 29% and improving perceptual quality (JOD) by 66% on BecomingLit. A static 3DGS reconstruction probe further confirms that our generations are the most multi-view consistent. Built on a video prior, VDAs produce effects beyond the reach of explicit renderers, including physically plausible hair dynamics, shadows, reflections, and refractions.
authors: Simon Giebenhain, Tobias Kirschstein, Liam Schoneveld, Davide Davoli, Zhe Chen, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner
bullets: Addresses the difficulty of reproducing video diffusion models’ rich appearance, motion, and physics priors with explicit 3D methods.
Fine-tunes a video diffusion model using disentangled learned expression codes and proxy-mesh renderings for independent control.
Uses a camera-triplet training strategy and public multi-view data to improve efficiency.
Outperforms prior single-image 3D avatars on novel-view reenactment, with lower face LPIPS and higher perceptual quality on BecomingLit.
Produces effects difficult for explicit renderers, including plausible hair dynamics, shadows, reflections, and refractions.
papers.selection_reason: Fine-tunes video diffusion models for controllable, multi-view consistent 3D avatar generation, directly fitting the video diffusion subtopic.
papers.title: Video Diffusion Avatars: Taming Video Diffusion Models into Controllable 3D Avatars
papers.tldr: Video Diffusion Avatars turn a single image into a photorealistic, multi-view-consistent 3D avatar with controllable viewpoint, expression, and upper-body pose.

papers.abstract: On AWS Trainium2, every component of a diffusion model runs as a program compiled ahead of time for fixed shapes, while pipelines differ across models, prompt lengths across requests, and caching decisions across denoising steps. We present Difflet, a serving engine in which five model pipelines share one compilation backend, joint attention is split across cores by attention head, and a host controller decides at each denoising step whether to run the denoiser or reuse its earlier output. A small probe program computes the caching signal on the device and returns one number per step, and a resident model process keeps every program loaded across requests. Across five image and video model families, fused attention accelerates denoiser steps by 1.2-4.3x over the same framework using PyTorch/XLA attention, and at 32.8k visual tokens it is the only attention that compiles. On four of the five models, resident serving is 1.5-3.4x faster than standalone runs that reload weights from a warm file cache for each generation.
authors: Bin Ma, Min Yu, Vijay Kodamalla, Jialin Liu, Dong Li
bullets: Addresses fixed-shape compilation constraints across varying pipelines, prompt lengths, and denoising-time caching decisions.
Uses one compilation backend for five pipelines, splits joint attention across cores by head, and fuses attention computation.
A host controller selectively reuses denoiser outputs, guided by a device-side probe that produces one caching signal per step.
Fused attention is 1.2–4.3× faster than PyTorch/XLA attention and is the only attention variant compiling at 32.8k visual tokens.
Resident serving is 1.5–3.4× faster than reloading weights for each generation on four of five models.
papers.selection_reason: Presents Difflet, a fast inference engine for diffusion transformer models on AWS Trainium, optimizing attention computation and caching to improve serving efficiency.
papers.title: DIFFLET: A Fast Inference Engine for Diffusion Transformer Models on AWS Trainium
papers.tldr: Difflet speeds diffusion-transformer inference on AWS Trainium2 through shared compilation, fused attention, adaptive caching, and resident model serving.

papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have become a common backbone for high-quality text-to-image and text-to-video generation, but repeated dense self-attention remains a major inference bottleneck as token sequences grow and the same operator is invoked across many denoising steps. Our study suggests that dense attention in pretrained DiTs contains reusable layer/head-specific high-mass structure that can be identified from a small offline calibration set and reused across future generations. This leads to Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention, a train-free attention replacement that reuses static sink masks and supplements them with a lightweight pooled-KV branch, while leaving model weights and sampling schedules unchanged. On Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, the method attains 1.54$\times$ end-to-end speedup while maintaining generation quality. On Z-Image-Turbo, it attains 1.57$\times$ end-to-end speedup with competitive GenEval2 performance. These results indicate that reusable importance-aware sparse support can provide an effective train-free acceleration path for both T2V and T2I DiTs.
authors: Bingxin Xing, Yu Zhang, Jiatong Ding, Lei Lu, Ping Wang
bullets: Targets the inference cost of repeated dense self-attention in DiTs with long token sequences and many denoising steps.
Uses small offline calibration to identify reusable, layer/head-specific high-mass attention structure.
Combines static sink masks with a lightweight pooled-KV branch as a train-free attention replacement.
Achieves 1.54× end-to-end speedup on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B while maintaining generation quality.
Achieves 1.57× end-to-end speedup on Z-Image-Turbo with competitive GenEval2 performance; scope covers T2V and T2I DiTs.
papers.selection_reason: Train-free sparse attention replacement for efficient T2I/T2V diffusion transformers.
papers.title: Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers
papers.tldr: Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention accelerates pretrained text-to-image and text-to-video diffusion Transformers by reusing calibrated sparse attention structure without retraining or changing sampling schedules.

papers.abstract: Large-scale diffusion models are commonly trained with a constant learning rate (LR) and exponential moving average (EMA), despite the strong performance of LR decay and Schedule-Free optimization in training large language models. We study whether EMA is uniquely suited to diffusion training, or whether stronger alternatives have been underexplored. Our theory shows that averaging a constant-step trajectory has an inherent optimization limitation, whereas LR decay and Schedule-Free optimization admit vanishing stationarity guarantees under standard nonconvex assumptions. Empirically, LR decay and EMA provide complementary benefits: combining decay with EMA further improves the standard baseline at most tested starting points, although the gain remains sensitive to when decay begins. Schedule-Free avoids this timing requirement and consistently outperforms EMA with a constant LR across training stages, achieving both lower fixed-evaluation objectives and better generation quality. Our analysis further shows that all three strategies substantially reduce parameter variability, yet stronger stabilization is not always better: EMA with a constant LR retains comparatively higher parameter variability, while aggressive decay combined with EMA achieves the lowest checkpoint variability but also weakens continued optimization. Schedule-Free substantially reduces parameter variability while preserving more late-stage progress, providing a better balance between parameter stability and continued optimization. Finally, the benefits of Schedule-Free extend beyond pretraining to ReFL and generator-side DMD, demonstrating its transferability across distinct diffusion optimization settings. Overall, our results suggest that large diffusion models need more than parameter averaging alone: effective optimization requires balancing variance reduction with continued optimization.
authors: Chuyu Hu, Huanran Chen, Shitong Shao, Yinpeng Dong
bullets: Constant-step EMA has theoretical optimization limits, while learning-rate decay and Schedule-Free optimization support vanishing stationarity guarantees under standard nonconvex assumptions.
Learning-rate decay and EMA are complementary, but decay’s benefit depends sensitively on when it begins.
Schedule-Free consistently outperforms constant-LR EMA across training stages in both fixed-evaluation objectives and generation quality, without requiring decay timing.
Aggressive decay with EMA minimizes checkpoint variability but can hinder continued optimization; Schedule-Free reduces variability while preserving late-stage progress.
Schedule-Free also transfers to ReFL and generator-side DMD, suggesting applicability beyond diffusion pretraining.
papers.selection_reason: Optimization study for large diffusion models with findings transferable to video diffusion training.
papers.title: Large Diffusion Models Need More Than EMA
papers.tldr: Large diffusion models benefit from optimization strategies beyond constant learning rates plus EMA, with Schedule-Free optimization offering a strong balance between stability and continued progress.

papers.abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) is a standard component of conditional diffusion models, and guided generation performance has become the \textit{de facto} measure of state-of-the-art models. Recent work on latent diffusion models seeks to learn latent spaces that are easier to model with diffusion. However, under CFG, generation additionally depends on how conditions are arranged in the latent space. We study this arrangement under discrete class conditions, termed \emph{class geometry}, and investigate what class geometry allows a latent space to work well with CFG. Under a Gaussian class model, we show that shifting variance from intra- to inter-class at fixed total variance makes classes more distinguishable under noise, and derive a noisy posterior objective whose per-sample descent direction is proportional to the oracle CFG correction. Based on the analysis, we propose Prototype Regularization (PR), a lightweight surrogate for the intractable noisy posterior objective, which applies a cosine prototype classifier to spatially pooled latents. With a controlled training budget (20 epochs for VAE, 80 epochs for DiT), adding PR to an LDM baseline reduces guided gFID on ImageNet from 3.31 to 2.28, surpassing a DINOv3-aligned VA-VAE (2.44) with negligible overhead. We further demonstrate that PR generalizes to pseudo-labels derived from clustering, continuous text-embedding conditions, and video latents. Together, our findings highlight class geometry as a critical factor in guided generation and take a first step toward CFG-compatible representation learning. Our project page is available at: https://maps-research.github.io/cfg-geometry/.
authors: Haoming Liu, Junhao Zhu, Shaoyi Zheng, Yuanhe Guo, Jinnuo Liu, Shenji Wan, Hongyi Wen
bullets: Motivation: CFG performance depends not only on diffusion modeling but also on how conditions are arranged in latent space.
Analysis: Under a Gaussian class model, increasing inter-class variance relative to intra-class variance improves class distinguishability under noise.
Method: Prototype Regularization (PR) approximates a noisy-posterior objective using a cosine prototype classifier over spatially pooled latents.
Result: Adding PR reduces ImageNet guided gFID from 3.31 to 2.28 with negligible overhead under the stated training budget.
Scope: PR also works with clustering-based pseudo-labels, continuous text embeddings, and video latents.
papers.selection_reason: Studies latent geometry for classifier-free guidance in diffusion models and demonstrates extension to video latents, directly relevant to video diffusion.
papers.title: Learning to Be Guided: Shaping Latent Geometry for Classifier-Free Guidance
papers.tldr: The paper shows that shaping latent class geometry improves classifier-free guidance (CFG) and proposes a lightweight prototype regularizer to make representations more CFG-compatible.

papers.abstract: Creative intent in video editing can be expressed through text instructions (e.g., "remove the people"), image references (e.g., subject appearance), video references (e.g., camera movement), or a combination of the above. We introduce OmniXRef, a unified framework for multimodal multi-reference video editing that allows users to combine variable numbers of text, image, and video references to control diverse attributes of a source video. We first devise a unified input design with a reference-bank interface and introduce $R^2$-RoPE to support generalization to more references. Then our model, OmniXRef-Model, uses a single-stream diffusion transformer to jointly process the source video and multimodal context from an MLLM in an interleaved sequence. To address the scarcity of training data for video-reference editing, we construct OmniXRef-Data using synthesis pipelines for different editing tasks and combinations of references. We use curriculum learning to progressively increase task complexity and resolution. To support systematic evaluation of video as a control modality, we introduce OmniXRef-Bench, a benchmark for video-reference attribute transfer across Camera, Motion, Content, Style, and Visual Effects (VFX). Comprehensive evaluations show that our OmniXRef-Model outperforms task-specific baselines and commercial models.
authors: Xiaoyan Cong, Tianyu Wang, Hyeonho Jeong, Zhifei Zhang, Yuqian Zhou, Yijun Li, Shaoteng Liu, Zhe Lin, Srinath Sridhar, Soo Ye Kim
bullets: Addresses the challenge of controlling video edits with variable combinations and numbers of multimodal references.
Uses a reference-bank interface, R²-RoPE for reference scalability, and a single-stream diffusion transformer with MLLM-derived context.
Builds synthetic OmniXRef-Data and applies curriculum learning to handle limited video-reference editing data and increasing task complexity.
Introduces OmniXRef-Bench for evaluating video-reference attribute transfer across camera, motion, content, style, and VFX.
Reports better performance than task-specific baselines and commercial models in comprehensive evaluations.
papers.selection_reason: Unified multimodal multi-reference video editing with a diffusion transformer, directly relevant to video diffusion and editing.
papers.title: OmniXRef: A Unified Framework for Multimodal Multi-Reference Video Editing
papers.tldr: OmniXRef unifies text, image, and video references for flexible, multi-attribute video editing in one framework.

papers.abstract: Recent advances in video generation let users create high-quality videos from natural language descriptions, yet obtaining results that match user intent remains time-consuming: individual generations are computationally expensive, and underspecified prompts force repeated cycles of generation, inspection, and revision. Existing video prompt optimization methods improve generation through automatic rewriting, but cannot supply the ideas and preferences that were not in the initial description. We propose ProactGen, a video generation framework that learns proactive clarification, eliciting user intent through questions grounded in generated video drafts. Specifically, we train a vision-language model as a questioning policy with reinforcement learning: observing the initial prompt and a video draft, it learns to ask the questions most valuable to downstream generation, rewarded by the alignment between the final generated video and a target reference. We further find that effective questioning does not require drafts of final-output quality, and exploit this property by generating drafts with fewer denoising steps, keeping the added cost of clarification low. Experiments show that ProactGen improves target alignment over direct generation by at least 1.8x the gain of the strongest baselines. Moreover, a single round of ProactGen already exceeds the alignment that the strongest baseline reaches after four refinement rounds, in 29% of its time.
authors: Zhixiao Wang, Yang Chen, Yifan Xu, Chenbin Li, Yue Chang, Kai Long, Fengming Dong, Limin Wang
bullets: Addresses underspecified prompts that otherwise require costly generate–inspect–revise cycles.
Uses a vision-language model trained with reinforcement learning to ask questions based on the initial prompt and a video draft.
Questions are optimized for their value to downstream generation, using final-video alignment to a target reference as the reward.
Low-cost drafts with fewer denoising steps keep clarification overhead small.
A single round outperforms the strongest baseline’s four-round refinement alignment in 29% of the time, and achieves at least 1.8× its alignment gain over direct generation.
papers.selection_reason: Learns proactive clarification for text-to-video generation with RL-trained questioning policies, directly relevant to video diffusion and prompt refinement.
papers.title: ProactGen: Learning Proactive Clarification for Video Generation
papers.tldr: ProactGen improves text-to-video alignment by proactively asking users targeted questions about draft videos before final generation.

papers.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have increased the demand for reliable watermarking for copyright protection, yet the robustness of video watermarks against removal attacks remains underexplored. Most watermark-removal methods originate from the image domain: signal optimization injects imperceptible pixel-domain perturbations, whereas generative resynthesis produces a visually similar instance through diffusion synthesis. When extended to videos, the former introduces temporally varying noise that causes visible flickering, while the latter regenerates fine-grained structures inconsistently across frames, leading to structural motion inconsistency. To evaluate video watermark robustness, we propose PoseRegen, a pose-consistent reconstruction framework that removes watermarks while preserving the original content and motion. PoseRegen first applies a temporally shared viewpoint transformation to disrupt watermark-bearing spatial patterns and then jointly reconstructs the transformed sequence with a pose-conditioned video model. A frozen video DiT processes the complete sequence with its reference-video latent, and full-sequence Flow Matching supervision keeps identity and background consistent across frames. To further preserve motion structure, we introduce a lightweight Pose-Conditioned Motion Consistency Adapter that adapts the frozen backbone to temporally ordered pose guidance and constrains body-part trajectories throughout reconstruction. Experiments on eleven video watermarking schemes show that PoseRegen reduces the average bit accuracy to 0.505, near random guessing, while outperforming the strongest baseline by 9.34% on motion-related VBench metrics. These results reveal a practical vulnerability of current video watermarks and highlight the need to evaluate robustness jointly with temporal and motion quality.
authors: Yifan Liao, Zhen Sun, Zhicong Huang, Jiaming He, Zongmin Zhang, Xi Ai, Cheng Hong, Xinhu Zheng, Xinlei He
bullets: Existing image-based removal methods cause video flicker or inconsistent structure when applied frame by frame or through resynthesis.
PoseRegen uses a temporally shared viewpoint transformation followed by pose-conditioned, full-sequence reconstruction.
A frozen video DiT with Flow Matching preserves reference content, while a motion adapter constrains pose and body-part trajectories.
Across 11 watermarking schemes, watermark bit accuracy falls to 0.505—near random guessing—and motion-related VBench scores improve by 9.34% over the strongest baseline.
The work emphasizes evaluating watermark robustness together with temporal and motion quality.
papers.selection_reason: Uses a frozen video diffusion transformer with flow matching for temporally consistent watermark removal, fitting diffusion-based video editing.
papers.title: Erase the Mark, Preserve the Motion: Temporally Consistent Removal of Video Watermarks
papers.tldr: PoseRegen removes video watermarks while maintaining temporal, identity, background, and motion consistency, exposing weaknesses in current watermarking schemes.

papers.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.
authors: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan, Haowen Xu, Liangliang Zhao, Ruixun Liu, Yuhan Wang, Yuwei Zhang, Liang Feng, Junhao Xiao, Kaiyan Zhang, Xuekai Zhu, Daizong Liu, Biqing Qi, Yihao Liu, Ganqu Cui, Ning Ding, Linfeng Zhang, Jianjun Li, Kun He, Xiang Bai, Bowen Zhou
bullets: Identifies limitations of conventional diffusion models in reasoning, autonomous exploration, and complex human-aligned objectives.
Presents a technical panorama of RL’s roles in diffusion models, emphasizing trajectory optimization and reward engineering.
Evaluates representative RL post-training strategies across multiple task-specific benchmarks.
Highlights three deployment bottlenecks: fragile reward design, exploration–exploitation challenges, and instability under sparse rewards.
Proposes a roadmap for robust, interpretable RL-driven diffusion systems and provides a public resource repository.
papers.selection_reason: Reviews RL-driven post-training for diffusion models, including multimodal and generation settings directly relevant to diffusion-based video generation.
papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
papers.tldr: This paper reviews and empirically analyzes how reinforcement learning post-training makes diffusion models more goal-directed, adaptable, and aligned across language, vision, robotics, and scientific applications.

papers.abstract: Training-free object removal commonly redirects self-attention away from the target region, but on few-step distilled diffusion models this often leaves object-shaped residuals. We identify a temporal mismatch: a structured prediction forms inside the mask at the first forward, and the short trajectory offers few later chances to revise it, while attention rerouting acts mainly in later steps. Across four distilled backbones, magnitude-matched single-forward interventions show that background-directed state correction affects the final result more than attention rerouting. We therefore propose ReState, which corrects the masked clean prediction toward background evidence retrieved from the input using a noise-level-aware weight that vanishes at the final forward. ReState retains object-excluding attention as a complementary constraint and adds no denoiser evaluations. Across two paired benchmarks and two few-step backbones, ReState achieves the best masked PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS among training-free methods, improving PSNR by 3.17 dB on average over the strongest baseline. On OBER-Test, it also outperforms the 50-step attention-forcing reference on all three metrics at 6.7x lower latency. The same configuration transfers to two additional distilled backbones without retuning. Project page: https://tdrlee.github.io/ReState
authors: Donghwan Lee, Sanghyun Jo, Sihyun Kim, Ziseok Lee, Kyungsu Kim
bullets: Few-step diffusion models can preserve object-shaped artifacts because structured errors arise early, while attention rerouting acts mostly later.
ReState applies noise-level-aware state correction using background evidence from the input, with the correction fading at the final forward.
It retains object-excluding attention as a complementary constraint and requires no additional denoiser evaluations.
Across two paired benchmarks and two few-step backbones, it reports the best masked PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS among training-free methods, with a 3.17 dB average PSNR gain over the strongest baseline.
On OBER-Test, it surpasses a 50-step attention-forcing reference at 6.7× lower latency and transfers to two additional distilled backbones without retuning.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a method for object removal in few-step diffusion models. Few-step diffusion is a critical efficiency technique for video generation, and the noise-level-aware state correction mechanism is a novel technical contribution applicable to this domain.
papers.title: ReState: Noise-Level-Aware State Correction for Training-Free Object Removal in Few-Step Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: ReState improves training-free object removal in few-step diffusion models by correcting early masked predictions toward background evidence before later denoising steps.

papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation enables rectified-flow models with diffusion-transformer architectures to combine task-specific capabilities within a single student. However, matching model outputs does not guarantee that their internal representations are aligned, and it remains unclear where and when additional feature supervision is most useful. We analyze the teacher-student feature mismatch across Transformer blocks and denoising timesteps, and find that the mismatch is concentrated in deeper Transformer blocks during early denoising and persists after OPD distillation, indicating ineffective distillation. Motivated by this observation, we introduce FocusOPD, which augments the base OPD objective with token-wise directional feature alignment restricted to deep layers and early denoising steps. Across two rectified-flow backbones and multiple OPD objectives, FocusOPD improves capability transfer in compositional generation, text rendering, and preference-based evaluation. On the primary benchmark, it improves over DiffusionOPD from 0.953 to 0.967 on GenEval, from 23.797 to 23.944 on PickScore, and from 6.052 to 6.199 on LAION-Aesthetic. Ablations show that selective deep and early supervision is more effective and efficient than alignment over the full network and trajectory.
authors: Xinrui Lin, Shumin Wang, Suqi Song, Fan Li, Yanyong Zhang
bullets: Feature mismatches concentrate in deep Transformer blocks during early denoising and remain after conventional OPD.
The method adds token-wise directional feature alignment only in these deep layers and early timesteps.
Evaluated across two rectified-flow backbones and multiple OPD objectives for compositional generation, text rendering, and preference evaluation.
On the primary benchmark, GenEval rises from 0.953 to 0.967, PickScore from 23.797 to 23.944, and LAION-Aesthetic from 6.052 to 6.199.
Ablations indicate selective supervision is more effective and efficient than aligning the full network and denoising trajectory.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses distillation for diffusion models, a core technique in video generation. The focus on feature alignment in deep layers and early denoising steps offers insights into improving the efficiency and quality of diffusion-based video generation.
papers.title: FocusOPD: Structure-Guided On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: FocusOPD improves multi-teacher diffusion distillation by aligning deep-layer features during early denoising, yielding better capability transfer than standard OPD.

papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) dominate video generation but suffer from high inference cost due to the quadratic complexity of self-attention. Sparse attention mitigates this by skipping unnecessary computation in the attention matrix, but existing methods apply a fixed sparsity ratio throughout denoising and struggle to accurately determine which computations to skip. To address these limitations, we analyze attention dynamics through attention entropy and mean attention distance, and find that attention becomes increasingly concentrated across denoising steps. We further observe that blocks selected early continue to capture a large fraction of the total attention weight at later steps. These findings suggest two acceleration opportunities: the sparsity ratio should grow as denoising progresses, and earlier search results can be reused to reduce the search space. Based on these findings, we propose Growing Sparsity and Reduced Search (GSRS), a training-free framework that retains more computation early and progressively reduces it later, while restricting subsequent searches to an early candidate set to reduce search overhead. GSRS adopts Top-p selection for adaptive sparsity control, supported by a precise evaluation scheme that computes exact attention weights within the FlashAttention computation at negligible overhead. Experiments on HunyuanVideo and Wan 2.1 validate that GSRS achieves 1.55$\times$--2.21$\times$ speedup while maintaining generation quality comparable to full attention.
authors: Yun Dai, Yuyun Chen, Jiarui Wen, Huiping Zhuang, Cen Chen, Ziqian Zeng
bullets: Video DiTs are slowed by quadratic self-attention, while fixed-sparsity methods poorly reflect changing attention patterns during denoising.
Attention becomes increasingly concentrated over denoising steps, and early-selected blocks retain much of the later attention weight.
GSRS is training-free: it keeps more computation early, reduces it progressively, and restricts later searches to an early candidate set.
Top-p selection provides adaptive sparsity, with exact attention-weight evaluation integrated into FlashAttention at negligible overhead.
Validated on HunyuanVideo and Wan 2.1, GSRS delivers 1.55×–2.21× speedup while maintaining quality comparable to full attention.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free sparse attention acceleration for video diffusion with growing sparsity and reduced search; relevant to efficient video generation.
papers.title: Sparse Attention for Video Generation Acceleration via Growing Sparsity and Reduced Search
papers.tldr: GSRS accelerates video diffusion Transformers by progressively increasing attention sparsity and reusing early search results, achieving 1.55×–2.21× speedups with comparable quality to full attention.

papers.abstract: Real-time mobile volumetric video enables immersive free-viewpoint experiences, but delivering high-quality 3D content under constrained bandwidth and computation remains challenging. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) systems, such as V$^3$, enable efficient mobile streaming by encoding time-varying Gaussian attributes with commodity video codecs and hardware decoding. However, existing pipelines treat all Gaussians as frame-varying signals, which is poorly suited to full-scene content where large portions remain temporally stable. Our empirical study shows that frame-wise adaptation and video coding of all Gaussians cause quality degradation in complex full-scene content, particularly in temporally stable regions. To address this issue, we propose ResStreamGS, a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework that processes Gaussians according to their temporal behavior. ResStreamGS identifies residual-sensitive primitives through lightweight probe adaptation and reuses stable Gaussians within each Group of Pictures (GOP). Stable Gaussians are transmitted once per GOP, while only residual-sensitive Gaussians remain in the frame-wise hardware-decodable video stream. Experiments on complex full-scene volumetric videos show that ResStreamGS improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51--8.35~dB over a controlled V$^3$-style all-Gaussians baseline, reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5%, and achieves 30.883~FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.
authors: Haoran Liu, Di Wu, Wang Luo, Hengyuan Na, Miao Hu, Guocong Quan
bullets: Targets quality degradation and bandwidth/computation inefficiency when all Gaussians are treated as frame-varying.
Uses lightweight probe adaptation to identify residual-sensitive Gaussian primitives.
Transmits stable Gaussians once per GOP and keeps only residual-sensitive Gaussians in the frame-wise hardware-decodable stream.
On complex full-scene videos, improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51–8.35 dB and reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5% versus a controlled V$^3$-style baseline.
Reaches 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes ResStreamGS for efficient mobile volumetric video streaming using 3D Gaussian Splatting, addressing both 3D foundation models and video generation efficiency.
papers.title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming
papers.tldr: ResStreamGS improves mobile volumetric video streaming by separating temporally stable Gaussians from residual-sensitive ones, reducing payload while enhancing reconstructed quality and maintaining real-time performance.

papers.abstract: Text-to-video models often generate the visual concepts requested in natural language prompts but fail to satisfy their intended ordering, timing, and persistence requirements. We propose representing these requirements as specifications in a formal Temporal Logic, and introduce Temporal Specification Guidance (TSG), a training-free inference-time framework that turns temporal specifications into executable objectives for guiding video generation during sampling. TSG scores traces of visual concept evidence using differentiable quantitative semantics and uses the score's gradients to construct a specification-guided denoising direction. We instantiate this framework with video-text attention traces, efficient differentiable scores for Metric Temporal Logic, and gradient-derived attention biases. This instantiation requires neither an external concept classifier nor backpropagation through the video transformer. Its attention-steered forward pass yields a denoising direction that augments classifier-free guidance (CFG). On a benchmark of 220 prompts spanning 11 categories of temporal constraints, including ordered object entry and state transitions, this instantiation improves specification satisfaction accuracy over CFG by 9.5-20 percentage points across five models, with minimal memory overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of temporal specifications and differentiable satisfaction objectives as a flexible interface for controlling video generation.
authors: Avishree Khare, Hideki Okamoto, Bardh Hoxha, Georgios Fainekos, Rajeev Alur
bullets: Targets failures in event ordering, timing, and persistence despite correct visual concepts.
Represents requirements in Metric Temporal Logic and scores visual concept attention traces with differentiable semantics.
Uses score gradients to create attention biases and a denoising direction that augments classifier-free guidance.
Evaluated on 220 prompts across 11 temporal-constraint categories and five models, improving satisfaction accuracy by 9.5–20 percentage points over CFG.
Requires no external concept classifier or backpropagation through the video transformer, with minimal memory overhead.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free temporal specification guidance for text-to-video diffusion models.
papers.title: Temporal Specification Guidance for Text-to-Video Generation
papers.tldr: Temporal Specification Guidance steers text-to-video sampling with formal temporal constraints, improving the correct timing and ordering of generated events without extra training or external classifiers.

papers.abstract: Unified multimodal generation covers discrete, continuous, and hybrid paradigms. Discrete approaches with single-codebook visual tokenizers align naturally with text modeling but have limited representational capacity. Continuous and hybrid approaches retain richer visual representations, but they model text and images in heterogeneous spaces with different training objectives, potentially introducing optimization conflicts between modalities with misaligned representation spaces. These choices expose a central question: how to efficiently model high-capacity visual representations alongside textual content in a shared optimization space within a single backbone. We present Intern Lumina U2, to our knowledge the first diffusion language model to represent multi-codebook visual tokens in a fully discrete space. Each visual position is represented by a group of codes from complementary codebooks, increasing its representational capacity while preserving compatibility with discrete text modeling. At the input, the embeddings are concatenated at each position; at the output, a lightweight multi-codebook autoregressive head predicts the codes within each position sequentially, while the diffusion backbone processes all positions in parallel. Built on the unified 4D representation of AToken, Intern Lumina U2 supports image, video, and 3D inputs within a single backbone and achieves leading performance among unified models in visual understanding, image generation, and image editing. We further build a full-stack training, inference, and evaluation system on both Ascend and NVIDIA platforms to verify the cross-platform effectiveness of our model. We also improve the inference efficiency through a stability-aware sampling strategy, which combines confidence-plateau-guided unmasking approach with drift-triggered cache refreshing mechanisms, accelerating image generation by 4.45x.
authors: Qian Yu, Zongyang Qiu, Juncheng Yan, Hongliang Li, Qi Qin, Keqi Wang, Siqi Luo, Junkui Ju, Yapeng Mi, Tiantian Lu, Tian Liu, Pengyu Xie, Chenhao Ji, Minghui Zhang, Yiang Zhao, Siyu Yan, Haiying Xu, Yanbo Wang, Jianghan Shen, Yuandong Pu, Jiayi Lei, Borui Zhang, Jinxin Shi, Bo Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Shenglong Ye, Lixin Gu, Hongjie Zhang, Linghan Liu, Xinyuan Chen, Yuewen Cao, Lihe Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Junjun He, Qiangwei Liu, Qi Zhang, Yu Cheng, Tianfan Xue, Hui Xiong, Chang Xu, Yu Qiao, Yihao Liu, Bin Fu
bullets: Addresses the limited capacity of single-codebook visual tokenizers and the optimization mismatch of hybrid continuous–discrete multimodal models.
Represents each visual position with complementary code groups, concatenating their embeddings and predicting codes sequentially with a lightweight head while denoising positions in parallel.
Built on AToken’s unified 4D representation to support image, video, and 3D inputs.
Reports leading performance among unified models for visual understanding, image generation, and image editing.
A stability-aware sampling strategy reportedly accelerates image generation by 4.45×, with cross-platform validation on Ascend and NVIDIA systems.
papers.selection_reason: Diffusion language model with multi-codebook discrete visual tokens for unified visual understanding and generation; relevant to multimodal foundation models and diffusion-based visual generation.
papers.title: Intern Lumina U2: A Multi-Codebook Diffusion Large Language Model for Omni-Visual Understanding and Image Generation
papers.tldr: Intern Lumina U2 is a diffusion language model that uses multiple discrete visual codebooks to unify text, image, video, and 3D understanding and generation in one backbone.

papers.abstract: Sampling from continuous flow-based generators such as flow matching models requires numerical ODE or SDE integration, making inference cost depend on the number of function evaluations (NFEs). In practice, the sampling budget is inherited from prior work or selected through expensive FID-versus-NFE sweeps, using FID to assess image-generation quality, requiring sample generation and evaluation at multiple budgets. This makes sampling-budget selection dependent on repeated empirical evaluation. We therefore ask a complementary question to solver design and timestep allocation: for a fixed pretrained model and solver, what numerical resolution is sufficient? We introduce FLOWBUDGET, a training-free estimator of solver-relative sampling complexity. Using simulation-free interpolation probes of the learned dynamics, FLOWBUDGET normalizes the leading one-step discretization error by the motion, estimates its coefficient from interpolation probes, and maps a numerical tolerance to a step budget using the solver order. We derive estimators for numerical solvers in flow~matching sampling, namely Euler and Heun for ODE sampling and additive-noise Euler--Maruyama for SDE sampling, and connect the ODE coefficients to terminal integration error. Experiments on SiT, FlowDCN and Rectified Flow models, spanning flow-model architectures and formulations, test whether FLOWBUDGET can estimate the NFE budget without generating samples at multiple budgets or performing an FID-versus-NFE sweep. The code is available at https://github.com/Yasaman-dt/FlowBudget
authors: Zahra Dehghani, Pablo Piantanida, Mohammadhadi Shateri
bullets: Addresses the costly, empirical selection of numerical resolution for pretrained flow-based generators.
Uses training-free, simulation-free interpolation probes of learned dynamics to estimate normalized one-step discretization error.
Derives budget estimators for Euler and Heun ODE solvers and additive-noise Euler–Maruyama SDE sampling.
Maps a target numerical tolerance to an NFE budget using solver order and relates ODE estimates to terminal integration error.
Evaluated across SiT, FlowDCN, and Rectified Flow models and formulations.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses efficiency in generative models by estimating sampling budgets for flow matching, a technique relevant to both video generation and efficient inference.
papers.title: FlowBudget: Training-Free Sampling-Budget Estimation for Flow Matching Models
papers.tldr: FLOWBUDGET estimates the sampling NFE budget needed by flow-matching models without repeated sample generation or FID-versus-NFE sweeps.

papers.abstract: Representation-alignment methods effectively accelerate the diffusion transformer training. REPA, for example, uses a pretrained vision encoder to supervise an intermediate layer through an MLP projection head which is discarded after training. It aims to import semantics from the vision encoder to the diffusion backbone. While this objective is achieved at early layers by back-propagating the alignment loss, there is no guarantee that later layers, supervised by the velocity prediction loss alone, can well access such semantics. We propose a simple solution, representation conditioning (RECON), to improve semantics in later layers. During training, we feed the pretrained vision encoder tokens into later layers; during inference, because we no longer have the clean image, we reuse the MLP head (as a proxy to the vision encoder) and project its output tokens to the later layers. Our method adds no parameters and leads to much faster convergence: RECON is $63\times$ faster than SiT and $25\times$ faster than REPA. Code is available at https://github.com/saeidrazavi/RECON
authors: Saeed Razavi, Xingjian Leng, Liang Zheng
bullets: REPA aligns early diffusion layers with a pretrained vision encoder, but later layers may not access those semantics effectively.
RECON feeds vision-encoder tokens into later layers during training.
At inference, it reuses the discarded MLP projection head as a proxy for the vision encoder to generate conditioning tokens.
The method adds no parameters and reports convergence 63× faster than SiT and 25× faster than REPA.
Code is publicly available on GitHub.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes Representation Conditioning (RECON) to improve semantics in later layers of diffusion transformers by reusing vision encoder tokens. This offers a training efficiency improvement for video/image diffusion models.
papers.title: Representation Conditioning for Generation
papers.tldr: RECON conditions later diffusion-transformer layers on pretrained vision representations, improving semantic access and substantially accelerating convergence without adding parameters.

papers.abstract: Interactive video generation commonly relies on small bidirectional chunks to reduce response latency. Yet our preliminary experiments show that larger chunks improve video quality and better utilize GPU parallelism, allowing more latents to be sampled with only a modest increase in sampling time. Motivated by these observations, we propose Speculative Sampling, a strategy that combines the modeling power of large bidirectional windows with the low-latency interaction of small ones. It expands the modeling window by appending noise latents as padding and caches the resulting predictions for reuse when the condition remains unchanged. Predictions are delivered incrementally, while the uncommitted future remains replaceable. Our latency analysis shows that this removes the waiting-time lower bound imposed by chunk boundaries, shifting the optimization focus from reducing chunk size to accelerating per-chunk sampling. Bidirectional window size thus becomes a decision variable for jointly optimizing visual quality and sampling time, rather than a necessary constraint on low-latency interaction. This opens a path to serving large bidirectional models in interactive streaming systems without complex streaming post-training.
authors: Yubo Huang, Yuxuan Zhang, Jiaming Liu, Sirui Zhao, Enhong Chen
bullets: Interactive video systems use small bidirectional chunks for responsiveness, but larger chunks can improve quality and GPU utilization.
The method expands the modeling window with noise padding and reuses cached predictions when conditions remain unchanged.
Video predictions are delivered incrementally while uncommitted future content remains replaceable.
The approach removes the waiting-time lower bound caused by chunk boundaries, shifting focus to faster per-chunk sampling.
It supports serving large bidirectional models for interactive streaming without complex streaming-specific post-training.
papers.selection_reason: Speculative sampling strategy for low-latency interactive video generation.
papers.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
papers.tldr: Speculative Sampling enables low-latency interactive video generation with larger bidirectional windows by caching predictions from noise-padded future latents.

papers.abstract: We present KinoGen, a framework that synthesizes customizable humanoid loco-manipulation references through kinematically grounded video generation. KinoGen conditions a pretrained video generator on calibrated renders of the target robot and object in a simulated task instance and recovers the reference by fitting the same models to the generated two-view video, so that the reference lies in the robot configuration space by construction without a human body proxy or retargeting. Body, hand, and object priors initialize the reconstruction, and direct optimization against cross-view evidence refines it. Since an edited keyframe is simply another rendered state, a user can prescribe a goal object pose, regenerate the video around the edited keyframe, and obtain a reference that satisfies the pose exactly. Across eight loco-manipulation tasks, KinoGen yields lower penetration and foot skating than video-based baselines and preserves over 90% of annotated contacts, and its customized references satisfy every prescribed target with substantially less penetration than direct interpolation. Tracking policies trained on the synthesized references are deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. Project webpage: https://kinogen-humanoid.github.io/.
authors: Qi Wu, Lulu Zhao, Sanghyun Hahn, Rishi Yennu, Emmy Yang, Dingqi Zhang, Tao Pang, Jiuguang Wang, Kuan Fang
bullets: Conditions a pretrained video generator on simulated renders of the target robot, object, and task.
Reconstructs robot and object motion by fitting the same models to generated video, avoiding human-body proxies and retargeting.
Supports exact goal-pose customization by editing a keyframe and regenerating the surrounding video.
Across eight tasks, reduces penetration and foot skating versus video-based baselines while preserving over 90% of annotated contacts.
References satisfy prescribed object poses and support deployment of tracking policies on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands.
papers.selection_reason: Uses video generation to synthesize kinematically grounded robot references for loco-manipulation.
papers.title: KinoGen: Customizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation References via Kinematically Grounded Video Generation
papers.tldr: KinoGen generates customizable, physically grounded humanoid loco-manipulation references directly in robot configuration space from calibrated two-view video.

papers.abstract: Autoregressive generation underlies real-time, causal video synthesis and is the backbone of video world models. Today's dominant approach distills a bidirectional diffusion model into a causal few-step student, but existing pipelines make this conversion prohibitively expensive, requiring offline Probability Flow ODE} (PF-ODE) trajectories that cost tens of thousands of GPU-hours and terabytes of storage. We show it can be made dramatically more efficient. Pushing this efficiency to its extreme, we reduce trajectory supervision to a single sample, the strictest setting possible, and find that it causes severe quality collapse. We trace this to the teacher's trajectory geometry: the high-noise regime, governing semantic layout and motion, and the low-noise regime, governing fine texture exhibit fundamentally different curvature and optimization behavior, so a single monolithic student cannot jointly fit both, causing severe representation interference. Motivated by this, we propose Glance Forcing, a lightweight distillation framework that decouples the denoising trajectory into two complementary slow and fast experts, each guided by a tailored, stage-specific objective, while keeping the pretrained teacher entirely frozen. This decoupling further reveals a general mechanism underlying few-step distillation: PF-ODE distillation mainly straightens the few-step trajectory geometry, while the subsequent distribution-matching stage independently governs distributional quality. Using only one PF-ODE trajectory, Glance Forcing already surpasses the fully-trained state-of-the-art baseline, raising the VBench Total score from 84.04 to 84.22 while cutting trajectory-collection cost from thousands of GPU-hours to about one A100-GPU-hour, with markedly larger gains in dynamic degree, VisionReward, and instruction-following, and consistent preference from human raters over strong baselines.
authors: Zhuobai Dong, Junchao Yi, Hu Jian Guo, Linjie Li, Rui Zhao, Alex Jinpeng Wang
bullets: Existing causal distillation pipelines require tens of thousands of GPU-hours and terabytes of PF-ODE trajectory data.
The authors attribute single-sample quality collapse to different optimization geometry in high-noise semantic/motion and low-noise texture regimes.
Glance Forcing uses two frozen-teacher-guided slow and fast experts with stage-specific objectives to decouple these regimes.
With one PF-ODE trajectory, it raises VBench Total from 84.04 to 84.22 and reduces trajectory collection to about one A100-GPU-hour.
It also reports gains in dynamic degree, VisionReward, instruction following, and human preference over strong baselines.
papers.selection_reason: Efficient distillation of bidirectional diffusion into an autoregressive few-step student for real-time video synthesis, with major cost reductions.
papers.title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance
papers.tldr: Glance Forcing efficiently distills bidirectional diffusion into autoregressive video generation using just one PF-ODE trajectory while improving quality over a fully trained baseline.

papers.abstract: Pairwise preference feedback has become a widely adopted supervision signal for reinforcement learning in video generation models, as pairwise comparisons provide a more reliable alternative than pointwise scalar ratings for evaluating the quality of generated videos. Specifically, we define a preference graph for each GRPO group under a pairwise evaluator, where nodes represent sampled rollouts and edges encode pairwise preferences. Auditing 6,976 on-policy comparison graphs, we find that cyclic preferences are prevalent and persist throughout training. Naive pairwise reward aggregation based on average win rates discards the underlying comparison structures and treats each rollout independently, which may introduce unreliable advantage estimates for certain rollouts and consequently affect reinforcement learning optimization. Therefore, we propose the \emph{Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk} (\ours{}), a graph-aware advantage aggregation method that strengthens the global preference signal from win rates with reliable relational evidence from cyclic preference graphs through a reliability-guided preference walk. Under matched evaluator, comparison protocol, group size, prompt schedule, and query budget, \ours{} requires no additional evaluator queries beyond the observed comparisons within each rollout group and improves over Pairwise-GRPO across controlled comparisons, transfer settings, and blind human evaluations.
authors: Xinrui Lin, Fan Li, Shumin Wang, Dehong Kong, Yanyong Zhang
bullets: Pairwise preferences for video rollouts often form cycles, which persist during training.
Win-rate aggregation ignores relational structure and can yield unreliable rollout advantages.
Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk combines global win rates with reliability-guided evidence from preference graphs.
It uses only comparisons already observed within each rollout group.
