The method improves over Pairwise-GRPO in controlled, transfer, and blind human evaluations, according to the abstract.
papers.selection_reason: Graph-aware preference aggregation for RL fine-tuning of video generation models, relevant to video diffusion training.
papers.title: When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO
papers.tldr: A graph-aware preference-walk method uses cyclic pairwise-comparison structure to produce more reliable advantages for video GRPO without extra evaluator queries.

papers.abstract: We present Kandinsky S2V 1.0, an open family of speech-to-video models for controllable audio-driven human animation, comprising Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite (2B parameters) and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro (21B parameters). From a single reference image, a speech waveform, and a text prompt, the models generate long-form 25 FPS video in which lip motion, expression, pose, and gesture follow the speech. The architecture draws text and audio conditioning from one Qwen2.5-Omni model and adds a reference-aware three-scale visual memory. Training starts from the Kandinsky 5.0 Video foundation models [1] and combines mixed reference-memory layouts with an area-adaptive face loss. The training corpus contains 1.17M single-speaker clips selected by active-speaker detection, with captions generated directly in English and Russian. A side-by-side human evaluation against the strongest open-source baseline and two proprietary commercial models shows that Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro performs comparably to or better than these models on average and is also preferred for lip synchronization. On common speech to video benchmarks, Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro rank among the top performing models according to mean rank over five reported metrics. Beyond the base models, we provide {\pi}-Flow distilled variants of both Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro. The distilled Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro model generates video in 16 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance, achieving a 5.4 times end-to-end speedup over the base model, while matching or exceeding it on nearly all reported benchmark metrics. To accelerate open research and deployment in speech-to-video generation, we release the code, model checkpoints, and diffusers integration under the MIT license.
authors: Nikolay Semenov, Artem Riabinin, Sergey Bassenko, Anna Averchenkova, Julia Agafonova, Anastasia Aliaskina, Kirill Kozlov, Lev Novitskiy, Nikita Samsonov, Nikolai Gerasimenko, Denis Dimitrov
bullets: Generates long-form 25 FPS avatar video from one image, speech waveform, and text prompt.
Uses unified text/audio conditioning, three-scale reference-aware visual memory, and area-adaptive face loss.
Includes Lite (2B) and Pro (21B) models trained on 1.17M active-speaker clips.
Pro performs comparably to or better than evaluated open and proprietary models, with preferred lip synchronization; both rank highly on common benchmarks.
π-Flow distillation enables the Pro model to generate in 16 steps without classifier-free guidance, delivering a reported 5.4× end-to-end speedup while largely preserving quality.
papers.selection_reason: Audio-driven avatar video generation, relevant to video diffusion and generation.
papers.title: Kandinsky S2V 1.0: Audio-Driven Avatar Video Generation
papers.tldr: Kandinsky S2V 1.0 is an open speech-to-video family that animates a reference image with synchronized speech-driven lip motion, expressions, poses, and gestures, with strong benchmark performance and a faster distilled variant.

papers.abstract: Memory for long-horizon video generation must satisfy two competing requirements: it must remain bounded so generation can continue indefinitely, while still recovering what was observed at a place when the camera returns, regardless of how long ago it was seen. Reconstruction-based memories provide spatial recall by caching and reprojecting explicit geometry, but require growing storage and depend on estimated 3D structure. Recurrent memories keep a constant-size state, but retention is governed by temporal recurrence, causing old observations to fade with time. We introduce SMART, a slot memory addressed by region tokens, which combines bounded storage with spatially addressed recall. SMART stores content in a constant-size slot recurrence whose writes are addressed by the observing camera and whose reads are queried by the rendering camera, without constructing an explicit 3D representation or maintaining a growing cache. Consequently, recall is conditioned on inter-view geometry rather than on recency. Each read additionally provides a confidence estimate that conditions a chunk-causal diffusion transformer, allowing it to selectively trust retrieved content while relying on its generative prior elsewhere. On long trajectories in Memory Maze and Minecraft, SMART maintains high-fidelity recall far beyond its training horizon while using constant memory and per-step cost.
authors: Eren Cetin, Julius Erbach, Vukasin Bozic, Hyojun Go, Zixiang Zhao, Nikolai Kalischek, Federico Tombari, Konrad Schindler, Dominik Narnhofer
bullets: Addresses the trade-off between bounded memory and recalling observations when the camera revisits a location.
Uses a constant-size slot recurrence with writes keyed by the observing camera and reads queried by the rendering camera.
Avoids explicit 3D reconstruction and growing caches by conditioning recall on inter-view geometry.
Provides confidence estimates to a chunk-causal diffusion transformer, which balances retrieved content with its generative prior.
On Memory Maze and Minecraft trajectories, maintains high-fidelity recall beyond the training horizon with constant memory and per-step cost.
papers.selection_reason: Bounded spatially addressed memory for long-horizon video generation, relevant to video world models and embodied memory.
papers.title: Long-horizon Video Generation with Slot Memory Addressed By Region Tokens
papers.tldr: SMART enables long-horizon video generation with constant memory by retrieving past visual content based on spatial camera regions rather than recency.

papers.abstract: Dense cardiac dynamics are essential for assessing cardiac function, yet in practice clinicians often observe only extremely sparse measurements. However, recovering full dynamics from such sparsity is a highly ill-posed problem due to the lack of temporal cues. While auxiliary time-series signals like ECG provide physiological guidance, effectively exploiting them is challenging due to the cross-modal representation gap and phase misalignment. In this work, we present CardioFAD, a Focus--Align--Diffuse paradigm that reformulates sparse cardiac dynamic synthesis as a recoverability--alignability anchor discovery problem. Our core insight is that resolving extreme temporal ambiguity requires a compact set of anchor states that are both sufficient to recover the visual trajectory and reliable for ECG--visual alignment. We therefore learn motion-salient keyframes under two complementary principles: trajectory sufficiency, which preserves trajectory-critical intra-modal motion content, and anchor alignment, which promotes consistent inter-modal correspondence at these anchors. We implement the Focus and Align modules optimized by the two aspects. Diffuse then performs two-stage generation by first synthesizing keyframes and subsequently interpolating the remaining frames. Extensive experiments on cardiac MRI and echocardiography videos demonstrate superior visual quality, temporal coherence, and improved functional consistency under the extreme one-shot regime.
authors: Junkai Liu, Haofan Wu, Nay Aung, Joao A. C. Lima, Steffen E. Petersen, Le Zhang
bullets: Addresses the severe temporal ambiguity of cardiac dynamic synthesis from extremely sparse observations.
Learns motion-salient keyframes that are both trajectory-sufficient and aligned with ECG signals.
Uses a Focus–Align–Diffuse pipeline: identify keyframes, align visual and physiological information, then generate keyframes and interpolate remaining frames.
Experiments on cardiac MRI and echocardiography show improved visual quality, temporal coherence, and functional consistency in the one-shot setting.
papers.selection_reason: Presents CardioFAD, a Focus-Align-Diffuse paradigm for synthesizing cardiac dynamics from sparse observations using ECG guidance. This applies video diffusion techniques to medical time-series data.
papers.title: Focus, Align, and Diffuse: Time-Series-Aware Keyframe Diffusion for Cardiac Dynamic Synthesis from Sparse Observations
papers.tldr: CardioFAD reconstructs dense cardiac motion from a single observation by selecting ECG-aligned motion keyframes and diffusing the missing frames.

papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanism behind why diffusion models memorize their training data remains an open question in generative modeling. In this paper, we examine this question from two perspectives: (a) the model-level perspective concerning the onset of memorization in a model during training, and (b) the sample-level perspective concerning the proclivity of an individual sample to be memorized by a given model. We show that the so-called input loss curvature, or the Frobenius norm of the Hessian of the diffusion model's training loss, is an effective metric for quantifying both perspectives on memorization. In particular, we empirically demonstrate that input curvatures averaged across training and validation samples can identify when a model is likely to start regurgitating its training data when tracked over training time. However, this metric is not sufficient for measuring an individual sample's likelihood of being memorized. To address this perspective, we introduce a counterfactual definition of memorization in diffusion models, extending the analogous notion from supervised learning proposed by [Feldman, 2019]. We prove that this counterfactual memorization is controlled by the input curvature of the leave-one-out model, thus establishing a direct theoretical link between a sample's local loss landscape and its generation likelihood. We validate our derived bounds through several empirical experiments and show that input-dependent curvature provides a proxy for memorization.
authors: Shashank Sule, Xinyue Yu, Boonam Shin, Yuxuan Liu, Abolfazl Hashemi, Hayden Schaeffer
bullets: Memorization is studied both as a training-time model behavior and as an individual sample property.
Average input curvature over training and validation samples can signal when a model begins regurgitating training data.
Curvature alone does not adequately measure whether a specific sample will be memorized.
The paper defines counterfactual memorization for diffusion models and proves it is controlled by input curvature of a leave-one-out model.
Experiments validate the theoretical bounds and support input-dependent curvature as a memorization proxy.
papers.selection_reason: Investigates memorization in diffusion models using loss curvature, providing a theoretical and empirical framework for understanding generative model behavior.
papers.title: Loss Curvature as a Sampling-Free Proxy for Memorization in Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: Input loss curvature, measured via the diffusion-loss Hessian, is a sampling-free proxy for detecting model-level memorization and estimating sample-level memorization under a counterfactual definition.

papers.abstract: Video diffusion models generate visually compelling short-term sequences but often struggle to preserve scene geometry and object structure over time. In this paper, we first demonstrate that current video attention cannot identify reliable correspondences across frames, with responses dispersed across multiple regions even after recognizable scene structure has emerged. We argue that reliable cross-frame associations are essential for information exchange as scene structure forms in video generation. Thus, we introduce Geometry Attention Distillation (GAD), which transfers correspondences from a frozen geometry model's attention to video attention. Extracted from clean videos, these correspondences link the same static surface or moving object across frames. Since structure formation begins in deeper layers at higher noise and shallower layers at lower noise, we apply attention distillation at a student layer selected according to the noise timestep. After training, video attention focuses more consistently on corresponding locations. Experiments across all three video backbones demonstrate improved long-range scene consistency and dynamic temporal consistency, with geometric gains across generation lengths. On Wan2.2 5B, GAD improves cross-frame matching accuracy by at least 30% over the Wan baseline on both long-range benchmarks. Notably, GAD achieves these gains without additional inference modules, offering a promising approach to efficient and consistent video-based world simulation. Project page: https://fantasy-amap.github.io/GAD/.
authors: Junfeng Ni, Ziyu Zhu, Fan Jiang, Yu Liu, Chiyu Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Zhaoxu Sun, Mu Xu, Siyuan Huang, Yixin Chen
bullets: Video diffusion models often lose scene geometry and object structure over time because their attention produces dispersed cross-frame correspondences.
GAD transfers attention correspondences from a frozen geometry model trained on clean videos to video attention.
Distillation targets a noise-timestep-dependent student layer, reflecting how structure forms from deeper to shallower layers during generation.
Across three video backbones, GAD improves long-range scene and dynamic temporal consistency across generation lengths.
On Wan2.2 5B, it improves cross-frame matching accuracy by at least 30% over the baseline on both long-range benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Video diffusion model improved with geometry attention distillation for consistent long-range generation.
papers.title: GAD: Geometry Attention Distillation for Consistent Video Generation
papers.tldr: GAD distills geometric cross-frame correspondences into video diffusion attention, improving long-range scene and object consistency without extra inference modules.

papers.abstract: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.
authors: Jiawei Zhang, Ziyu Wan, Nanye Ma, Long Zhao, Dong Chen, Hongyu Liu, Qifeng Chen, Dongdong Chen
bullets: Uses on-policy velocity regression as the foundation for few-step distillation.
Introduces Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that captures teacher velocity variation within coarse transitions.
Repels the student from weaker teacher predictions to reduce undesirable modes.
Evaluated across image, 3D, video, and joint audio–video generation, including models up to 33B parameters.
Supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation; reports outperforming strong few-step baselines and surpassing multi-step teachers on several benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Few-step diffusion distillation reduces sampling cost and is evaluated on video synthesis, fitting video diffusion and efficient inference.
papers.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
papers.tldr: SMD simplifies few-step diffusion distillation into a regression-based method that achieves strong 4-NFE generation without auxiliary score models or deployment-time architecture changes.

papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models have emerged as a foundation for long-horizon world rollout. However, when extended far beyond their training windows, these models suffer from progressive drift: visual quality deteriorates, motion becomes inconsistent, and object identity gradually collapses as generated frames are recursively reused as context. We study a supervision-horizon gap: short-horizon distillation leaves later rollout states without direct supervision. We show that matching short-window marginals need not determine long-horizon behavior, while longer on-policy trajectories expose delayed failures to training. This motivates temporal manifold matching at scale for long-horizon world models. Building on this insight, we introduce LongForcing, a distillation approach that scales teacher supervision to long student self-rollouts. LongForcing preserves the short-horizon teacher-forcing and causal ODE-distillation stages, while replacing the realscore teacher in the final distribution-matching stage with an extended-horizon bidirectional teacher. The long-horizon teacher supervises extended student self-rollouts using the standard distribution-matching formulation, without modifying the student architecture or increasing inference cost. We evaluate LongForcing on text-to-video generation and interactive action-conditioned world models, achieving a VBench Quality score of 85.52 and improving WorldRoamBench 60s action score by 23.9 points in first-person ablations. Qualitative stress tests further sample interactive rollouts up to 24 hours, far beyond the training horizon. These results suggest that scaling supervision along the temporal axis is a practical step toward long-horizon world models. The project website and code are at https://github.com/Fantasy-AMAP/LongForcing.
authors: Ziyu Zhu, Zhaoxu Sun, Fan Jiang, Mengchao Wang, Junfeng Ni, Ting-Bing Xu, Zhicheng Liu, Mu Xu
bullets: Targets progressive visual degradation, motion inconsistency, and object-identity collapse beyond the training horizon.
Identifies a supervision-horizon gap: short-window distillation does not constrain delayed rollout failures.
Extends temporal manifold matching by replacing the final-stage realscore teacher with an extended-horizon bidirectional teacher.
Preserves the student architecture and inference cost while supervising long self-rollouts.
Reports a VBench Quality score of 85.52, a 23.9-point improvement on the WorldRoamBench 60s action score in first-person ablations, and qualitative rollouts up to 24 hours.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes long-horizon world rollout via temporal manifold matching for autoregressive video diffusion, directly relevant to world models and video generation.
papers.title: LongForcing: Scaling Temporal Manifold Matching for Long-Horizon World Rollout
papers.tldr: LongForcing reduces long-horizon video and world-model drift by training on extended student self-rollouts with a bidirectional teacher.

papers.abstract: Post-hoc linearization is an attractive way to accelerate pretrained Video Diffusion Transformers (Video DiTs), yet existing methods largely treat the quality loss induced by attention replacement as a recovery problem. We show that a more fundamental bottleneck lies upstream: \emph{initialization}. Random initialization discards pretrained knowledge, whereas manual weight reuse transfers it through rigid and incomplete source--target correspondences. We introduce \textbf{LinMorph}, which recasts Video DiT linearization as a learnable softmax-to-linear weight transformation problem. Instead of copying predefined counterparts, LinMorph learns a cross-parameter morphism that lets each target Gated DeltaNet (GDN) parameter draw jointly from pretrained query, key, value, and output projections, including for parameters with no direct softmax counterpart. A single morphism is shared across layers and learned through local teacher alignment, while producing layer-specific initializations from their respective pretrained weights. The resulting weights are then materialized as independent GDN modules for progressive distillation and joint recovery.Since the morphism operates in weight space rather than token space, it can be learned on short, low-resolution clips and directly reused at larger video scales. Across pretrained Video DiTs, LinMorph enables markedly faster recovery and better final generation quality than random initialization and heuristic weight reuse. Results show that efficient linearization depends not only on how a converted model is recovered, but critically on how pretrained knowledge is transferred before recovery. Project page: https://lonelyling.github.io/LinMorph.
authors: Lingyi Long, Congyue Zhao, Xiaoou Li, Yanmin Qian, Tao Huang
bullets: Identifies initialization—not only post-conversion recovery—as a key bottleneck in Video DiT linearization.
Learns a shared cross-parameter softmax-to-linear morphism instead of relying on random initialization or rigid weight copying.
Allows each GDN parameter to combine information from pretrained query, key, value, and output projections, including unmatched parameters.
Uses local teacher alignment on short, low-resolution clips, then applies layer-specific transformed weights for progressive distillation and recovery.
Reports faster recovery and better final generation quality across pretrained Video DiTs than random or heuristic initialization.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a weight-morphing method to linearize Video Diffusion Transformers, improving efficiency of video DiT inference.
papers.title: LinMorph: Learning to Morph Weights for Efficient Video DiT Linearization
papers.tldr: LinMorph learns how to transfer pretrained attention weights into linear Gated DeltaNet modules, enabling faster Video DiT linearization with better recovered quality.

papers.abstract: Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) have recently emerged as a powerful framework for unified text-vision synthesis, surpassing traditional U-Net architectures in generative tasks. One key innovation lies in its Multimodal Self-Attention (MM-SA) interaction, where image and text tokens are concatenated and processed via self-attention. However, this mechanism poses significant challenges for editing, rendering conventional U-Net-based attention manipulation methods ineffective. To address this limitation, we propose QK-Edit, a training-free framework that exploits the unique attention dynamics of MM-DiTs for precise text-guided image and video editing. By introducing a novel query-key manipulation strategy, our method isolates and adjusts critical attention components to achieve an optimal balance between prompt fidelity and structural consistency. This enables seamless edits across various tasks, including object addition, object removal, object replacement, changing background, changing material, changing color, and style transformation. Notably, it can be easily implemented with feature replacement in inference. QK-Edit demonstrates superior editing performance on state-of-the-art models, such as FLUX and HunyuanVideo, effectively bridging the gap between generative power and editable flexibility in MM-DiTs, and paving the way for scalable multimodal content creation.
authors: Tiancheng Shen, Zilong Huang, Xiangtai Li, Zhijie Lin, Jiyang Liu, Yitong Wang, Jiashi Feng, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Jun Hao Liew
bullets: Addresses the difficulty of applying conventional U-Net attention-editing methods to MM-DiTs with concatenated image-text tokens.
Manipulates query-key interactions to balance prompt fidelity with preservation of the original structure.
Supports object addition, removal, replacement, background and material changes, color edits, and style transformations.
Implemented through feature replacement during inference, without additional training.
Demonstrates effective editing on MM-DiT models including FLUX and HunyuanVideo.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free attention manipulation for image/video editing in MM-DiTs; directly relevant to diffusion-based editing in video models.
papers.title: QK-Edit: Revisiting Attention-based Injection in MM-DiT for Image and Video Editing
papers.tldr: QK-Edit is a training-free query-key attention manipulation framework that enables precise text-guided image and video editing in MM-DiTs.

papers.abstract: High-fidelity surgical video generation is increasingly important for surgical education, simulation, and downstream AI training, as conventional simulation pipelines are limited by cost, realism, and scenario diversity. Adapting generic text-to-video diffusion models to surgical procedures remains difficult, however, due to complex anatomical structures, intricate tool-tissue interactions, the inherently hierarchical nature of surgical workflows, and the scarcity of curated training data outside a few well-studied procedures. We propose a surgical video generation framework that combines hierarchical procedural annotation with curriculum transfer learning. Surgical procedures are decomposed into three levels (phase, task, and action) and a pretrained text-to-video diffusion model is progressively adapted from coarse to fine-grained surgical context, supported by a dynamic sampling strategy that handles variable-resolution and variable-length surgical clips. We instantiate the framework on Bilateral Axillo-Breast Approach robotic thyroidectomy, a procedure for which no curated benchmark currently exists. Relative to the preceding task-level model, the final action-level model reduces FVD by 20.1% and FID by 15.7%, and a matched-budget ablation indicates that these gains arise from the curriculum design rather than from additional training. A user study with six clinicians rates visual realism highly while highlighting remaining gaps in anatomical accuracy and clinical reliability. The proposed framework offers a step toward AI-driven surgical simulation in procedures where curated data are scarce.
authors: Youngbin Kong, Seungho Lee, Jae Kyung Shin, Jong-hyuk Ahn, Hyoun-Joong Kong, Kyu Eun Lee
bullets: Addresses the difficulty of generating surgical videos with complex anatomy, tool–tissue interactions, hierarchical workflows, and scarce curated data.
Decomposes procedures into phase, task, and action levels, then progressively transfers these contexts into a pretrained text-to-video diffusion model.
Uses dynamic sampling to accommodate surgical clips with varying resolutions and lengths.

On Bilateral Axillo-Breast Approach robotic thyroidectomy data, the action-level model improves FVD and FID over the task-level model; matched-budget ablation attributes gains to the curriculum design.
Six clinicians rated visual realism highly but identified remaining limitations in anatomical accuracy and clinical reliability.
papers.selection_reason: Adapts text-to-video diffusion to surgical procedures with curriculum learning; fits video diffusion.
papers.title: Hierarchical Curriculum Learning for Surgical Video Generation: Focusing on Bilateral Axillo-Breast Approach Robotic Thyroidectomy Datasets
papers.tldr: A hierarchical curriculum adapts text-to-video diffusion models to generate realistic robotic thyroidectomy videos, improving visual metrics while leaving anatomical and clinical reliability challenges.

papers.abstract: Recent video super-resolution (VSR) models achieve efficient one-step generation through diffusion distillation. However, high-resolution inference remains costly, and distilled models are difficult to align with human preferences. These challenges call for improvements in both model architecture and training strategy. We present \textbf{FlashVSR+} to address both limitations. On the architecture side, we introduce hybrid attention based on the strong locality observed in pretrained VSR models, while retaining sparse global interaction for long-range consistency. It achieves up to $2\times$ DiT speedup and 45\% lower peak memory, enabling spatially untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090. On the training side, we propose Reward-Yield Distribution Matching Distillation (Ry-DMD) for preference-aligned one-step generation. Ry-DMD uses reward-weighted teacher rollouts to incorporate black-box rewards into distribution matching, without backpropagating through the reward model. We further show that Ry-DMD generalizes beyond VSR to T2I generation. Together, FlashVSR+ delivers stronger restoration quality and substantially improves high-resolution efficiency, with consistent gains in user preference. We release our code, models, and training data at \href{https://www.flashvsr.tech}{\textcolor{FlashBlue}{\textbf{www.flashvsr.tech}}}.
authors: Ruchang Yao, Shi Guo, Junhao Zhuang, Mingde Yao, Xin Cai, Jiahao Zhan, Bin Fu, Xinyuan Chen, Yu Qiao, Tianfan Xue
bullets: Targets the high inference cost of high-resolution VSR and the difficulty of aligning distilled models with human preferences.
Uses hybrid attention that emphasizes local interactions while preserving sparse global context for long-range consistency.
Introduces Reward-Yield Distribution Matching Distillation (Ry-DMD), which uses reward-weighted teacher rollouts without backpropagating through the reward model.
Reports up to 2× DiT speedup and 45% lower peak memory, enabling untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090.
Achieves stronger restoration quality and consistent user-preference gains; Ry-DMD also generalizes to text-to-image generation.
papers.selection_reason: Efficient video super-resolution via diffusion distillation and hybrid attention, relevant to video diffusion and efficient attention.
papers.title: FlashVSR+: Efficient Video Super-Resolution via Hybrid Attention and Reward-Yield Distribution Matching
papers.tldr: FlashVSR+ makes one-step video super-resolution faster and more preference-aligned through hybrid attention and reward-weighted distillation.

papers.abstract: Model providers can support image protection, but open-weight deployment introduces practical constraints. We propose four requirements: protection effectiveness, clean fidelity, compatibility, and tamper resistance. We incorporate long-horizon attack simulations to strengthen resistance to protection removal. Experiments with a single protection tool show improved resistance to re-alignment at a cost to clean fidelity, motivating further research toward practical model-side protection.
authors: Jihye Kang, Jiwon Park, Namhyuk Ahn
bullets: Open-weight deployment creates constraints beyond user-side image defenses.
Protection should balance effectiveness, clean fidelity, compatibility, and tamper resistance.
Long-horizon attack simulations are used to improve resistance to protection removal and re-alignment.
Experiments with one protection tool show stronger re-alignment resistance but reduced clean fidelity.
Further research is needed for practical model-side protection.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses image protection in open-weight diffusion models, proposing requirements and resistance to long-horizon attacks.
papers.title: Beyond User-Side Defenses: Image Protection in Open-Weight Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: The paper frames image protection for open-weight diffusion models around four practical requirements and strengthens tamper resistance through long-horizon attack simulations, though clean-image fidelity declines.

papers.abstract: Video world models must generate physically plausible futures, not just realistic frames. Existing approaches typically use semantic, physical, or predictive information to guide the visual generation stream, leaving a fundamental question: where inside the generator should predictions of scene evolution live? Standard video tokens jointly encode appearance and dynamics, but provide no distinct state for learning and reading predictive dynamics. We answer this question with the Physical Registry: temporally grounded registry slots inside a video DiT that are initialized from an observation-conditioned forecast, co-evolve with video tokens, and receive future-representation supervision, making predictive dynamics an explicit, readable state of the generator. In a controlled comparison of predictive-state interfaces on Physics-IQ Verified, Physical Registry improves vanilla fine-tuning by 9.9/8.7 points on I2V/V2V, the largest gain among the interfaces we compare. Across all Cosmos and WAN backbones, Physical Registry improves Physics-IQ Verified scores. With only 0.45% additional parameters, it enables Cosmos 3 Nano 16B to surpass the published I2V score of Cosmos 3 Super 64B (43.56 vs. 42.7). On WorldModelBench, it also improves physical adherence and the total score for all four evaluated backbones. Because the registry becomes candidate-specific while remaining readable, the Physical Registry Selector (PRS) ranks emerging futures by how far their intermediate registry readouts depart from the shared forecast before full denoising is complete. Across four backbones, this selection improves I2V scores by 5.6-15.9% without completed-video external scoring. Together, these results support a broader principle: dynamics prediction should live as an explicit model state that co-evolves with the video representation. Project page: https://grainsack.github.io/physical-registry/
authors: Shinseong Kim, Jaeseok Jeong, Jianlong Fu, Youngjung Uh
bullets: Video tokens normally mix appearance and dynamics without a distinct, readable state for scene evolution.
The method inserts temporally grounded registry slots into a video DiT, initialized from an observation-conditioned forecast and supervised with future representations.
Across Cosmos and WAN backbones, it improves Physics-IQ Verified and WorldModelBench performance; the abstract reports gains of 9.9/8.7 points for I2V/V2V in controlled comparisons.
With 0.45% extra parameters, Cosmos 3 Nano 16B exceeds the published I2V score of Cosmos 3 Super 64B.
The Physical Registry Selector ranks futures from intermediate registry readouts, improving I2V scores by 5.6–15.9% without completed-video external scoring.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces explicit predictive-state registry slots inside video diffusion world models, directly advancing physically plausible video prediction.
papers.title: World Models Need a Physical Registry: Learning Internal Predictive States for Physically Plausible World Models
papers.tldr: Physical Registry adds explicit predictive-state slots to video world models, improving physical plausibility and enabling early ranking of candidate futures.

papers.abstract: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models have emerged as powerful generative priors across domains ranging from molecular design to high-resolution image synthesis. However, standard diffusion sampling is inherently biased toward high-likelihood regions, often limiting the diversity of outputs. In many domains, a single, high-likelihood sample is insufficient. Instead, diverse portfolios of high-performing solutions are required, motivating methods that uncover a model's full expressive range. Here we show that integrating Quality-Diversity (QD) optimisation with diffusion models enables the discovery of diverse, high-performing outputs. We first propose Quality-Diversity Diffusion, a framework that adapts QD to diffusion models by directly optimising the model's latent noise and conditioning embeddings and leveraging embedding models to quantify diversity. Second, we introduce a novel h-space Spectral Mutation operator, which guides search along directions of maximal semantic sensitivity by analysing principal singular vectors of the model's input-to-activation Jacobian. We evaluate our combined approach, Spectral-Guided Quality-Diversity Diffusion, on text-to-image generation. Against 12 baselines, our method consistently achieves the lowest FID score, demonstrating an excellent balance of image quality and diversity.
authors: Hannah Janmohamed, Joao Correia, Penousal Machado, Antoine Cully
bullets: Standard diffusion sampling favors high-likelihood regions, limiting output diversity when portfolios of strong solutions are needed.
Quality-Diversity Diffusion optimizes latent noise and conditioning embeddings while using embedding models to measure diversity.
The h-space Spectral Mutation operator searches along semantically sensitive directions identified from principal singular vectors of input-to-activation Jacobians.
On text-to-image generation, the combined method achieved the lowest FID among 12 baselines, indicating a strong quality–diversity balance.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a spectral-guided quality-diversity framework for diffusion models, directly contributing to the Video Diffusion subtopic.
papers.title: Uncovering the Generative Landscape of Diffusion Models: A Spectral-Guided Quality-Diversity Diffusion Framework
papers.tldr: Spectral-Guided Quality-Diversity Diffusion searches diffusion-model inputs to generate diverse, high-quality images rather than only high-likelihood samples.

papers.abstract: Explicit point correspondence is attractive for adapting video generators: it describes how visible surfaces move, but can overwrite the appearance prior learned by a large pretrained model. We study this tension in a 5.01B-parameter text-to-video diffusion transformer. ACROSSVAM2.0 combines a confidence-weighted track-and-visibility head, zero-initialized residual feedback, and asymmetric PCGrad that removes only the auxiliary component opposing the primary flow-matching gradient on shared LoRA parameters. The design preserves the generator exactly at initialization and protects its primary update during adaptation. In a four-way ablation trained for 1,000 steps with three independent seeds, the full method lowers KLT forward-backward cycle error in all three seeds relative to a matched flow-only continuation (mean seed-level difference -0.00711, SD 0.00505), while robust sharpness remains positive in all three. An expanded 24-prompt evaluation (216 videos) yields 9.7% lower aggregate CoTracker3 cycle error than the matched control and near-matched performance on six VBench dimensions; however, the seed-level tracking effect is heterogeneous and I3D-FVD regresses from 0.1824 to 0.2022. These results support a bounded claim: conflict-aware adaptation improves correspondence consistency without broad perceptual degradation, but does not uniformly improve video quality. We release equations, pseudocode, matched outputs, source tables, and artifact provenance.
bullets: Addresses the tension between explicit surface-motion supervision and preserving a pretrained video generator’s appearance prior.
Combines confidence-weighted track/visibility prediction, zero-initialized residual feedback, and asymmetric PCGrad on shared LoRA parameters.
Preserves the generator exactly at initialization and protects the primary flow-matching update during adaptation.
Improves aggregate CoTracker3 cycle error by 9.7% versus a matched control, with near-matched performance across six VBench dimensions.
Tracking improvements are heterogeneous across seeds, and I3D-FVD regresses from 0.1824 to 0.2022; video quality is not uniformly improved.
papers.selection_reason: Adaptation of a text-to-video diffusion transformer with point correspondence supervision directly targets video diffusion.
papers.title: AcrossVAM2.0: Conflict-Aware Point Supervision for Parameter-Efficient Video Diffusion Adaptation
papers.tldr: AcrossVAM2.0 uses conflict-aware point supervision and parameter-efficient adaptation to improve video correspondence consistency while largely preserving pretrained video quality, though FVD worsens and tracking gains vary by seed.

papers.abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion enable novel-view video synthesis from a single input video, supporting world modeling, embodied intelligence, and robotic simulation. However, existing methods process camera trajectories independently, lacking the cross-trajectory consistency needed for coherent, navigable 4D worlds. We introduce Demiurge, an autoregressive video rerendering pipeline built on a dynamic 4D point-cloud memory cache. It promotes cross-trajectory consistency through four components: (1) an appearance video diffusion model that synthesizes photorealistic novel-view videos conditioned on the 4D memory; (2) a memory-consistent video depth completion model that aligns known-region depths with cached geometry and completes missing regions, mitigating scale ambiguity and discontinuities during memory updates; (3) memory-aware dual-stream warping that provides high-fidelity visual guidance and occlusion cues for novel-view synthesis; and (4) geometry-aware video refinement that enhances perceptual quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and three key capabilities: coherent spatiotemporal lattice construction over dense multi-view trajectories; large-parallax video rerendering under challenging camera motions, including 180-degree rotations with no input-view overlap; and geometry-faithful outputs that can be directly optimized into high-quality 3D Gaussian Splatting representations with minimal artifacts. Project page: https://hanxinzhu-lab.github.io/demiurge_project_page/.
authors: Hanxin Zhu, Jianqi Ma, Cong Wang, Zhihao Hu, Junyao Gao, Tianyu He, Junyan Lin, Jiayin Xiao, Jiateng Shou, Sen Liang, Weidong Zhang, Zhibo Chen, Jun Zhang
bullets: Addresses cross-trajectory inconsistency in existing novel-view video synthesis methods.
Combines appearance diffusion, memory-consistent depth completion, dual-stream warping, and geometry-aware refinement.
Supports coherent spatiotemporal reconstruction across dense multi-view camera trajectories.
Handles large-parallax motion, including 180° rotations without input-view overlap.
Produces geometry-faithful videos that can be optimized into high-quality 3D Gaussian Splatting representations with minimal artifacts.
papers.selection_reason: Autoregressive video rerendering with 4D memory for navigable worlds; fits world models, video generation, and 3D vision.
papers.title: Demiurge: Forging Navigable 4D Worlds via Autoregressive Video Rerendering
papers.tldr: Demiurge builds coherent, navigable 4D worlds from a single video by autoregressively rerendering novel views with a dynamic 4D point-cloud memory.

papers.abstract: Training-free sparse attention is a practical route to efficient video diffusion transformer inference, yet existing methods typically fix the competition domain at each query row for every attention head. Prior work primarily addresses how to estimate token-level importance within this fixed domain; whether the domain itself should adapt to head heterogeneity remains under-specified. We introduce EG-Sparse, a training-free framework that routes low-entropy heads to a grouped cross-head pool while retaining per-row local selection for high-entropy heads, using only scores already materialized by the sparse pipeline. A controlled diagnostic fixes the ranking score and varies only the competition rule: grouped cross-head selection reduces low-entropy-head reconstruction error by 9.8%, whereas forcing high-entropy heads into an all-head global pool increases it by 7.9%. Across four configurations, EG-Sparse achieves higher video quality while reducing attention density and GPU denoising latency compared with strong training-free sparse-attention baselines. Mechanism ablations further show that selective domain adaptation outperforms uniform, random, and fixed domain-assignment policies. These results support competition-domain adaptation as a distinct design axis within centroid-guided training-free sparse attention.
authors: Tiantian Liu, Meng Wan, Zhiqiang Liang, Jue Wang, Ningming Nie, Yangang Wang
bullets: Existing methods use a fixed competition domain for every attention head, despite head heterogeneity.
EG-Sparse routes low-entropy heads to grouped cross-head selection while keeping high-entropy heads on per-row local selection.
A controlled diagnostic found grouped selection reduced low-entropy-head reconstruction error by 9.8%, while global pooling increased high-entropy-head error by 7.9%.
Across four configurations, the method improved video quality while lowering attention density and GPU denoising latency versus strong training-free baselines.
Ablations favored selective domain adaptation over uniform, random, and fixed assignment policies.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free sparse attention for video diffusion transformers; fits efficient attention and video diffusion.
papers.title: Competition Domains Matter: Selective Head Globalization for Training-Free Sparse Attention in Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.tldr: EG-Sparse improves training-free sparse attention for video diffusion by adapting the token-selection competition domain to each head’s entropy.

papers.abstract: Can autoregressive video diffusion be accelerated further when only four denoising steps remain? Existing feature caching approaches struggle in this regime, as large feature changes between denoising timesteps undermine both direct reuse and lightweight predictors. We observe that features across video chunks remain strongly correlated at matching denoising timesteps, offering a complementary source of guidance. Building on this insight, we introduce TGuide, a framework that accelerates autoregressive video diffusion through a lightweight Anchor-Transport-Correct (ATC) predictor guided by historical sampling trajectories. Our ATC combines two complementary references: the current chunk's preceding-step features preserve its spatial structure, while the previous chunk's same-timestep features provide information at the target denoising stage. By integrating these references through spatial retrieval and adaptive correction, ATC improves velocity prediction accuracy despite the large gaps between denoising steps. To mitigate error accumulation across both denoising steps and video chunks, we train the predictor on its own autoregressive rollouts, allowing it to adapt to states shaped by its own earlier predictions. An optional confidence-aware scheduler further adjusts the quality-efficiency trade-off. Experiments on Self Forcing, Causal Forcing, and HY-WorldPlay show that TGuide preserves generation quality while achieving denoising speedups of up to $1.89\times$ over the original 4-step generators. On Self Forcing, TGuide generalizes from 81-frame training videos to 333-frame generation, approximately four times the training length, while exceeding the original model's VBench score.
authors: Zhuo Chen, Bin Zou, Fanyue Wei, Lixin Duan, Angela Yao, Wen Li
bullets: Addresses feature-caching failures caused by large changes between the few remaining denoising steps.
Uses an Anchor-Transport-Correct predictor combining the current chunk’s preceding-step features with the previous chunk’s same-timestep features.
Applies spatial retrieval and adaptive correction to improve velocity prediction across large denoising gaps.
Trains on its own autoregressive rollouts to reduce error accumulation across denoising steps and video chunks.
Evaluated on Self Forcing, Causal Forcing, and HY-WorldPlay; on Self Forcing, it generates 333-frame videos from 81-frame training videos while exceeding the original model’s VBench score.
papers.selection_reason: Accelerates autoregressive video diffusion via historical trajectory guidance; fits video diffusion, autoregressive video, and efficiency.
papers.title: TGuide: Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Historical Trajectory Guidance
papers.tldr: TGuide accelerates 4-step autoregressive video diffusion by guiding feature prediction with historical trajectories, achieving up to 1.89× denoising speedups while preserving or improving quality.

papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generators synthesize long videos through chunk-wise rollouts, yet they are typically trained to predict only the immediate future. This limited prediction horizon makes it challenging to maintain video quality over extended rollouts. To address this problem, we introduce Prospective Forcing, a multi-head prediction framework that injects long-range predictive signals into autoregressive video representations. Built on a rolling-window generator, Prospective Forcing attaches lightweight, offset-specific heads that share the same conditioning information and independently predict chunks at different future temporal offsets. By extending supervision beyond the next chunk, these heads encourage the shared history representation to retain information useful for longer-horizon prediction, supporting temporally consistent generation. At inference time, we accelerate sampling by using accepted future-chunk predictions to skip full-window backbone executions. We equip the head with learnable embeddings to generate multiple candidates for the next chunk, and a learned verifier either selects a candidate or rejects all and falls back to standard autoregressive generation.
authors: Yifan Shen, Yewei Xia, Gongxu Luo, Peiyuan Zhu, Boyang Sun, Zhenhao Chen, Guangyi Liu, Guangyi Chen, Kun Zhang
bullets: Addresses quality degradation in long video rollouts caused by training only on the immediate next chunk.
Uses lightweight, offset-specific prediction heads sharing the rolling-window generator’s conditioning information.
Extends supervision to multiple future offsets so representations retain longer-range predictive information.
Accelerates inference by accepting verified future predictions, while falling back to standard generation when candidates are rejected.
Supports multiple next-chunk candidates via learnable embeddings and a learned verifier.
papers.selection_reason: Directly addresses autoregressive long video diffusion with multi-head future prediction and sampling acceleration.
papers.title: Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion
papers.tldr: Prospective Forcing trains autoregressive video generators to anticipate multiple future chunks, improving long-horizon consistency while enabling faster inference through candidate verification and skipping.

papers.abstract: In film production, chroma keying composites an approved foreground performance into a new environment, but conventional workflows require coordinated background plates and dedicated harmonization. Recent generative methods often require pre-aligned backgrounds, focus on background-conditioned foreground relighting, or represent the environment only through an edited first frame. These restrictions limit background selection, scene composition, and camera motion while adding preparation or editing effort. We present FreeCHROMA, which adapts a pretrained video diffusion model in a parameter-efficient manner for generative video compositing from one to three unaligned background references. The model integrates the foreground into the referenced environment, preserving foreground identity, motion, and fine visual details while generating a spatiotemporally coherent background. Foreground-background harmonization occurs within the same generation process, without a separate relighting stage. Optional text instructions help disambiguate complex spatial relationships and camera behavior. To train the model, we construct pseudo-paired data from readily available real monocular videos through foreground-background separation and augmentation with existing foundation models. The original videos serve as training targets, while automated processing and quality verification enable scalable data construction. Across reference fidelity, foreground preservation, scene integration, harmonization, and overall video quality, FreeCHROMA consistently outperforms recent compositing and conditional video-generation baselines, with particularly clear gains under camera motion. FreeCHROMA relaxes the constraints of existing tools to enable end-to-end generative chroma keying from unaligned inputs, with exploratory experiments demonstrating its potential in robotics.
authors: Jiayi Wu, Tianfu Wang, Rui Zhao, Florian Schiffers, Zhimin Chen, Cornelia Fermuller, Yezhou Yang, Christopher Metzler, Yiannis Aloimonos
bullets: Addresses the need for coordinated background plates, manual harmonization, and restricted camera motion in conventional and recent generative compositing workflows.
Parameter-efficiently adapts a pretrained video diffusion model to integrate foregrounds into referenced environments and jointly perform background generation and harmonization.
Uses pseudo-paired training data built from real monocular videos via foreground–background separation, foundation-model augmentation, and automated quality verification.
Optional text instructions help resolve complex spatial relationships and camera behavior.
Reportedly outperforms recent compositing and conditional video-generation baselines across fidelity, preservation, integration, harmonization, and video quality, especially with camera motion.
papers.selection_reason: Adapts pretrained video diffusion for generative compositing, directly relevant to video diffusion.
papers.title: FreeCHROMA: Generative Chroma Keying from Unaligned Background References
papers.tldr: FreeCHROMA enables end-to-end video chroma keying from one to three unaligned background references while preserving foreground motion and identity and generating coherent, harmonized environments.

papers.abstract: Video diffusion models increasingly serve as priors for 4D generation, but the generated videos often lack geometric consistency. Recent approaches address this through post-training by designing geometric rewards, yet this can degrade texture and fine detail, requiring auxiliary appearance rewards and careful reward balancing. To address this challenge, we propose GeoFix, a unified framework that improves geometric consistency and visual quality with a single geometric reward, applicable to both training and inference-time reward alignment. Our reward measures cross-view depth consistency in static scene regions, targeting structural inconsistencies without directly constraining appearance or penalizing valid object motion. Crucially, depth agreement increases with camera field-of-view overlap even in real videos and 4D datasets, allowing a smaller camera movement to be mistaken for better geometry. We account for this effect by calibrating the reward against the overlap-dependent trend. GeoFix achieves a 39% improvement in WorldScore 3D consistency and a 4% increase in VBench Quality Score.
authors: Yeobin Hong, Hyojun Go, Dohun Lee, Jeongjae Lee, Sunghwan Hong, Federico Tombari, Zhaochong An, Jong Chul Ye, Konrad Schindler, Dominik Narnhofer
bullets: Addresses geometric inconsistency in video-diffusion-based 4D generation.
Uses one reward for both training-time and inference-time alignment, avoiding appearance-reward balancing.
Measures depth agreement in static scene regions while preserving valid object motion and appearance.
Calibrates for camera field-of-view overlap, which can otherwise make smaller camera movements appear geometrically better.
Reports a 39% improvement in WorldScore 3D consistency and a 4% increase in VBench Quality Score.
papers.selection_reason: Improves geometric consistency in 4D generation from video diffusion priors via a calibrated depth-consistency reward.
papers.title: GeoFix: Geometry Fixing for 4D Consistent Generation
papers.tldr: GeoFix improves 4D video generation by calibrating a cross-view depth-consistency reward to enhance geometry without sacrificing visual quality.

papers.abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) typically applies a shared scale to all latent tokens, although their velocity predictions evolve differently during sampling. We introduce Trajectory-Adaptive Classifier-Free Guidance (TrajCFG), a training-free method for flow-matching models that adapts token-wise guidance using historical changes in guided velocity direction. TrajCFG maps this feedback to bounded scales, assigning stronger guidance to larger directional changes and weaker guidance to more consistent directions. It combines adjacent-step and interval-normalized longer-span feedback, reusing standard CFG predictions without additional model evaluations. Controlled diagnostics and ablations examine the roles of directional feedback, token-wise allocation, and history-span fusion. Experiments on text-to-video, image-to-video, text-to-audio-video, text-to-image, and image-to-3D generation show improvements over base samplers across multiple backbones. For text-to-video generation, TrajCFG improves VBench Total scores by 0.30-0.75 points over the strongest evaluated baseline on each of three backbones. These results support historical directional feedback as a broadly applicable signal for fine-grained guidance allocation. The project page is available at https://jyliu-98.github.io/trajcfg-project-page/.
authors: Jingyu Liu, Hao Jiang, Yikang Ding, Huafeng Shi, Xu Yang, Xiaoqiang Liu, Guoxin Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai
bullets: Addresses the limitation of using one shared CFG scale despite different token-wise sampling dynamics.
Uses adjacent-step and longer-span trajectory feedback to assign stronger guidance to larger directional changes and weaker guidance to consistent directions.
Is training-free and reuses standard CFG predictions, requiring no additional model evaluations.
Evaluated across text-to-video, image-to-video, text-to-audio-video, text-to-image, and image-to-3D generation.
Improves text-to-video VBench Total scores by 0.30–0.75 points over the strongest evaluated baseline across three backbones.
papers.selection_reason: Token-wise classifier-free guidance for flow-matching video generation; directly relevant to video diffusion.
papers.title: TrajCFG: Token-Wise Classifier-Free Guidance via Denoising Trajectory Feedback
papers.tldr: TrajCFG improves classifier-free guidance by adapting the scale for each token according to historical changes in its guided velocity direction, without extra model evaluations.

papers.abstract: Accurate artery extraction from X-ray coronary angiography (XCA) is essential for coronary artery disease diagnosis and intervention. However, low vessel visibility, respiratory and cardiac motion, and limited annotations challenge existing methods. Moreover, most deep learning approaches produce binary vessel masks without preserving clinically relevant intra-arterial contrast information. We propose a Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model (TDBM) that formulates vessel extraction as image translation and learns from physics-informed synthetic data without manual vessel annotations. A physics-based XCA synthesis engine generates diverse, perfectly aligned pairs of contrast-enhanced and contrast-free images. Using these pairs, TDBM learns cross-domain mappings to recover high-fidelity vessel information. Temporal conditioning incorporates adjacent frames to improve consistency, while a vessel-aware contrastive loss exploits background-invariant synthetic pairs to enhance vascular discrimination. We evaluate TDBM on two XCA vessel segmentation datasets and conduct a reader study using two real-patient XCA sequence datasets. Zero-shot segmentation is further assessed on retinal imaging and fluorescence microscopy datasets. Results demonstrate that TDBM consistently outperforms existing methods and generalizes effectively across imaging modalities. Code and trained weights will be available at: https://github.com/Advanced-AI-in-Medicine-and-Physics-Lab/TDBM
authors: Jinkui Hao, Donald R. Cantrell, Ramez Abdalla, Sameer A. Ansari, Bo Zhou
bullets: Addresses poor vessel visibility, cardiac and respiratory motion, and limited annotated XCA data.
Generates aligned contrast-enhanced/contrast-free image pairs with a physics-based synthesis engine.
Uses temporal conditioning and vessel-aware contrastive learning to improve consistency and vascular discrimination.
Evaluated on XCA segmentation, real-patient sequence reader studies, and zero-shot retinal and fluorescence microscopy tasks.
Reports consistent improvements over existing methods and effective cross-modality generalization, without specifying numeric results.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model for vessel extraction that uses physics-informed synthetic data and temporal conditioning, bridging video generation and understanding.
papers.title: Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model for Vessel Extraction Using Physics-informed Synthetic Data
papers.tldr: TDBM uses physics-informed synthetic XCA pairs and temporal diffusion modeling to extract vessels while preserving intra-arterial contrast information without manual annotations.

papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) aim to automate the full experimental loop, from scientific decision-making to physical execution. Ideally, AI-generated plans could be carried out directly by robotic systems, but reliable automation remains difficult in complex, open-world laboratory environments, where experiments often involve fine-grained manipulation, long-horizon procedures, and substantial variation across tasks and setups. Humans therefore remain an important execution interface between AI-generated plans and physical experiments, creating a need for clear and effective human-facing experimental guidance. Because laboratory procedures are inherently visual, spatial, and dynamic, video is particularly well suited to communicating apparatus configurations, manipulation actions, temporal dependencies, and state changes. Recent advances in video generation now make it possible to synthesize experimental demonstrations directly from an initial workspace image and a natural-language instruction. However, whether such models can reliably communicate real laboratory procedures has not been systematically studied. We introduce LabInstruct, a benchmark for situated instructional video generation in real laboratories. LabInstruct contains 204 tasks across 5 scientific disciplines, with real reference executions and structured annotations of objects, actions, contacts, and state transitions. Evaluating 8 frontier image-to-video models, we find that visually plausible generations frequently remain procedurally incorrect, revealing a substantial gap between visual realism and the reliability required for experimental instruction.
authors: Yuming Fu, Weijia Wu, Jing Chen, Jiahao Tang, Feifei Chen, Hongyu Zhu, Xin Jin, Alex Jinpeng Wang
bullets: Targets the challenge of communicating complex, fine-grained, long-horizon lab procedures in self-driving laboratories.
Introduces 204 tasks spanning 5 scientific disciplines, with real reference executions and structured annotations.
Evaluates 8 frontier image-to-video models from an initial workspace image and natural-language instruction.
Shows a substantial gap between visually realistic videos and procedurally accurate experimental guidance.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for situated instructional video generation, relevant to video generation models.
papers.title: LabInstruct: Benchmarking Situated Instructional Video Generation for Lab Procedures
papers.tldr: LabInstruct benchmarks whether image-to-video models can generate reliable, human-facing videos for real laboratory procedures, finding that visual plausibility often does not ensure procedural correctness.

papers.abstract: We present HorizonNav, a video diffusion-based framework for anticipatory robot navigation that transforms a single RGB image and a text prompt into a geometrically aligned representation of plausible surrounding 3D space. Given the initial observation and a textual description of the reconstruction objective, a vision-language model, guided by designed instructions, interprets the scene and constructs structured prompts for a video diffusion model. The resulting video sequence provides plausible future observations of the environment, which are subsequently processed using monocular ORB-SLAM3 for camera pose estimation and Video Depth Anything for dense depth prediction. Our central contribution is a geometry-guided depth alignment stage that combines the estimated camera poses with triangulated visual landmarks to constrain dense depth predictions across multiple views. This alignment improves the geometric consistency of the reconstructed 3D environment, addressing inconsistencies that temporal coherence of the generated video alone cannot resolve. The experimental evaluation of navigation in imagined 3D environment shows that across a 19-scene horizon study, planning-feasible scenes increase from 13/19 at P20 to 15/19 at P81, while successful RRT trials increase from 62/90 to 75/90. In a separate corridor study, 6 of 25 evaluable generated-camera trajectories violate the reconstructed collision constraints; RRT planner recovers feasible alternatives in 5 of those 6 cases. A larger archive contains 58 usable reconstructions from 67 attempted cases, of which 36 support a downstream plan and 22 do not, exposing reconstruction and free-space failure modes rather than hiding them without lidar. Across 15 corridor reconstructions, the mean reconstruction error is approximately 0.30 m at matched structural landmarks.
authors: Hajira Amjad, Valerii Serpiva, Viacheslav Liubimov, Didar Seyidov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou
bullets: Generates plausible future views from one RGB observation plus a textual reconstruction objective.
Uses a vision-language model to guide prompts for video diffusion, then applies ORB-SLAM3 and Video Depth Anything.
Aligns dense depth with camera poses and triangulated landmarks to improve multi-view geometric consistency.
In a 19-scene horizon study, planning-feasible scenes rose from 13/19 to 15/19, and successful RRT trials from 62/90 to 75/90.
The approach remains subject to reconstruction and free-space failures; matched-landmark error was approximately 0.30 m across 15 corridor reconstructions.
papers.selection_reason: Video diffusion world model for anticipatory robot navigation with geometry-guided depth alignment.
papers.title: HorizonNav: Geometry-Guided Video Diffusion for Anticipatory 3D Robot Navigation
papers.tldr: HorizonNav uses text-guided video diffusion and geometry-based depth alignment to imagine and reconstruct navigable 3D surroundings from a single RGB image.

papers.abstract: Fewer latent tokens promise cheaper diffusion. Yet aggressive latent compression creates a reconstruction-generation dilemma: adding channels improves reconstruction but makes generation harder. We introduce APEX, short for Asynchronous Prefix denoising for EXtreme compression, which pairs a hierarchical latent space with asynchronous denoising over channel groups. Our autoencoder orders channel prefixes from structure to detail, while one shared denoiser generates them at staggered local times without adding tokens. On ImageNet-512, APEX outperforms existing methods at every evaluated channel count under 64x and 128x compression. At matched training and guided sampling compute, it also outperforms a 256-token model at every evaluated budget, with larger gains at lower compute. Code is available at https://daviddinkevich.github.io/APEX.
authors: David Dinkevich, Nisan Chiprut, Yoav HaCohen, Dani Lischinski
bullets: Addresses the reconstruction–generation trade-off in aggressively compressed latent spaces.
Uses an autoencoder with channel prefixes ordered from global structure to fine detail.
A shared denoiser generates channel groups at staggered local times without adding tokens.
On ImageNet-512, it outperforms prior methods across evaluated channel counts at 64× and 128× compression.
It also surpasses a 256-token model at matched compute, with larger gains at lower budgets.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a compression method for diffusion models using asynchronous denoising, improving efficiency in video generation and addressing token management.
papers.title: APEX: Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for Extreme Compression
papers.tldr: APEX enables extreme latent compression by asynchronously denoising hierarchical channel groups, improving image generation quality without increasing token count.

papers.abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tunes diffusion models with black-box rewards, but reverse-process methods such as Flow-GRPO are limited in efficiency by poor credit assignment, while forward-process methods such as DiffusionNFT are efficient yet unstable without carefully tuned exponential-moving-average (EMA) off-policy training. We show that NFT-style objectives contain a hidden forward--reverse consistency force that joint positive--negative training cancels only partially, and that EMA stabilizes training through restoration rather than off-policy rollouts. We introduce DiffusionART (Diffusion Reinforcement with Aggregation-First Reward Tilting), which aggregates each prompt's rewards into a shared reward-improving direction for reverse-process states, removing the consistency force by construction, and adds a trust-region-masked second update for drift-adaptive restoration without EMA tuning. It requires no differentiable reward model, remains effective with fewer samples per prompt, and supports pairwise reward models (DiffusionART-Pairwise). Across image and video generation, DiffusionART trains efficiently and stably without per-task tuning. In particular, on HunyuanVideo-13B with equally weighted visual and motion quality rewards, DiffusionART reaches the late-stage mean reward levels of DiffusionNFT and Flow-GRPO-Fast with 12.02 and 11.72 times fewer GPU hours, respectively, while achieving 28.8% and 53.0% higher mean training rewards.
authors: Zhenglin Wan, Jiayu Chen, Zhengfeiyang Zhang, Pengfei Zhou, Wangbo Zhao, Fangyuan Kong, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Yang You
bullets: Addresses inefficient credit assignment in reverse-process RL and instability in forward-process methods.
Aggregates per-prompt rewards into a shared reward-improving direction for reverse-process states, eliminating a conflicting consistency force.
Uses a trust-region-masked second update for drift-adaptive restoration instead of carefully tuned EMA training.
Requires no differentiable reward model, works with fewer samples per prompt, and supports pairwise rewards through DiffusionART-Pairwise.
Across image and video generation, it achieves comparable late-stage rewards with substantially fewer GPU hours and higher mean training rewards on HunyuanVideo-13B.
papers.selection_reason: Reinforcement-learning fine-tuning method for diffusion models, demonstrated on image and video generation.
papers.title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: DiffusionART is an efficient and stable online-RL method for fine-tuning diffusion models that improves reward optimization while avoiding EMA tuning and costly reverse-process training.

papers.abstract: Training-free feature reuse accelerates diffusion transformer inference by replacing full denoising computation at selected steps with cached approximations. Existing methods mainly improve the reconstruction of skipped features, but we find that once a stable first-order reconstructor is used, increasing reconstruction complexity brings limited gains, whereas the placement of exact-computation steps has a much larger effect on fidelity. More importantly, absolute shallow-probe variation is jointly affected by input-trajectory displacement and network response strength, and therefore does not directly reflect cache risk. We address this confounding by normalizing probe-output variation with the corresponding input displacement, yielding a directional gain per unit trajectory movement. Based on this signal, we propose CacheScope, which identifies high-risk reuse steps online and selectively falls back to full denoising computation while leaving the underlying cache reconstructor unchanged. CacheScope requires no additional training, gradients, auxiliary networks, or prompt-specific offline schedule optimization. Across FLUX.1-dev, Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, and Open-Sora 1.2, CacheScope achieves up to 3.57x acceleration and reduces median LPIPS by up to 70.1% over the strongest probe-based baseline.
authors: Qinhan Lyu, Jusheng Zhang, Zhixing Zhang, Hao Liu, Zijie Liang, Jin Jiang, Keze Wang
bullets: Exact-step placement matters more than increasing the complexity of a stable cache-feature reconstructor.
Raw shallow-probe variation confounds input-trajectory movement with network response strength and can misestimate cache risk.
CacheScope normalizes probe-output variation by input displacement to estimate directional gain per unit movement.
It selectively falls back to full denoising at high-risk steps while keeping the existing cache reconstructor unchanged.
Across three diffusion models, it reduces median LPIPS by up to 70.1% versus the strongest probe-based baseline.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes CacheScope, a method to accelerate diffusion transformer inference by identifying high-risk steps for exact computation, directly relevant to video diffusion acceleration.
papers.title: CacheScope: Exact-Compute Allocation for Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration
papers.tldr: CacheScope accelerates training-free diffusion inference by allocating exact computation to high-risk denoising steps identified through normalized probe variation, achieving up to 3.57× speedup with substantially better fidelity.

papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve remarkable performance in video synthesis, but their iterative denoising process suffers from high inference latency. To address this, caching has emerged as an effective acceleration strategy by capitalizing on inter-step redundancy during denoising. Existing dynamic caching methods typically estimate the error that cache reuse would introduce at each denoising step (step error) to guide cache decisions, whereas our concern is how much quality loss cache reuse would cause in the final generated video (terminal error). We show that step error does not directly correspond to terminal error and that latent information helps capture their relationship, thereby informing cache decisions. Moreover, existing threshold-based methods cannot provide precise speedup control, making it difficult to meet practical requirements for user-specified acceleration targets. To address these limitations, we introduce MORCA, a cache scheduling framework trained through offline-to-online reinforcement learning to make latent-aware reuse/recompute decisions under user-specified acceleration targets. Extensive experiments on different video generation models across multiple target acceleration ratios demonstrate that MORCA achieves better generation fidelity than state-of-the-art caching methods under comparable computational budgets. Code is available at https://github.com/x10ngyx/MORCA.
bullets: Existing caching methods optimize per-step error, which does not reliably reflect final video quality loss.
MORCA learns the relationship between latent information, cache decisions, and terminal generation error.
Its policy makes reuse-versus-recompute decisions under explicit acceleration targets, offering finer speedup control than threshold-based methods.
Experiments across multiple video generation models and acceleration ratios show better fidelity than prior caching methods at comparable computational budgets.
papers.selection_reason: RL-based cache reuse to accelerate video diffusion; fits efficient inference and video diffusion.
papers.title: MORCA: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Cache Reuse in Video Diffusion Acceleration
papers.tldr: MORCA uses latent-aware offline-to-online reinforcement learning to adaptively schedule cache reuse in video diffusion, improving fidelity while meeting user-specified acceleration targets.

papers.abstract: Video tokenizers have emerged as a cornerstone of modern video modeling, underpinning progress in compression, reconstruction and generation by mapping high-dimensional visual signals into compact latent spaces. However, despite this progress, current tokenization paradigms largely remain within the 2D visual domain, treating videos as image sequences rather than observations of an underlying dynamic 3D world. Consequently, the learned tokens inherit this observation-centric bias, limiting their capacity to compactly represent real-world 4D scenes. To mitigate this issue, we propose VideoTok4D, a novel 4D-aware video tokenizer for compact world representation. Specifically, our approach comprises three key designs: 1) a spatiotemporal disentanglement strategy that factorizes videos into static and dynamic tokens for holistic world modeling; 2) a track-aware dynamic attention mechanism that aggregates trajectory-aligned cues to promote cross-view motion consistency; and 3) Co4DGen, a diffusion prior learned over the resulting VideoTok4D token space for efficient 4D scene generation. Extensive experiments have demonstrated that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance while requiring up to 4 orders of magnitude less storage than dense 4D representations. Moreover, the compact token space substantially shortens diffusion sequences, enabling efficient generation.
bullets: Addresses the limitation of 2D, image-sequence-based video tokenizers for representing dynamic 3D worlds.
Disentangles videos into static and dynamic tokens for holistic world modeling.
Uses track-aware dynamic attention to aggregate trajectory-aligned cues and improve cross-view motion consistency.
Introduces Co4DGen, a diffusion prior over the token space for efficient 4D scene generation.
Reports state-of-the-art performance with up to 4 orders of magnitude less storage than dense 4D representations, while shortening diffusion sequences.
papers.selection_reason: 4D-aware video tokenizer for compact world representation and diffusion-based 4D generation.
papers.title: VideoTok4D: A 4D-Aware Video Tokenizer for Compact World Representation
papers.tldr: VideoTok4D builds a compact 4D-aware video tokenization framework that separates static and dynamic content, captures trajectory-consistent motion, and enables efficient 4D scene generation.

papers.abstract: On a film set, the camera move is committed during a take. Generative video reshooting lets filmmakers change it afterward, but may require hallucinating unrecorded content, a gap sometimes discovered only after leaving the set. We present Hybrid Cinematography, a workflow that bridges physical capture and generative reshooting to manage hallucination risk while filmmakers can still act on it. Using an editable 3D shot plan and a proxy of the take, our previsualization evaluates hallucination risk in real time. Seeing where the take lacks support, filmmakers can iteratively adjust the plan, explore moves that balance capture and generation, shoot guided pickups, or knowingly accept hallucination. We demonstrate the workflow through a mobile augmented reality application for on-set planning, capture, and review, and an offline pipeline for existing video. A study with experienced filmmakers reveals how previsualizing risk informs camera decisions and exposes tensions between creative intent and generative hallucination.
